title: fix(gemini): keep diagnostics and setup on the Gemini path
body:
## What and why

With `TALK_PROVIDER=gemini` and only a Gemini API key configured, the provider check passes but the auth check falls through to OpenAI/Codex. That false failure blocks `hermes talk check`, and setup can tell a Gemini user to run `codex login`. Unrelated OpenAI model and voice settings can also fail the Gemini report.

Route Gemini diagnostics and setup through the existing Gemini key/model/voice functions. The auth receipt now says: "Gemini API key is configured; live authentication was not checked." Update the human renderer and support-bundle allowlist together, so Gemini receipts need no Codex/xAI fields.

- Preserve scoped-key precedence and rejection of explicitly blank overrides.
- Report the actual Gemini model and case-sensitive voice; custom models retain an honest configuration-only warning.
- Keep setup repair prompts on Gemini settings and preserve per-write confirmation.
- Preserve existing OpenAI and Grok behavior.
- Update the operating guide and Unreleased changelog for the next patch release.

Fixes #122

## How to test

The new whole-report regression failed on the original source at the attempted OpenAI auth diagnostic. The candidate adds 19 cases covering key precedence, unrelated OpenAI settings, offline/no-write behavior, mixed receipt rendering, bundle key exclusion, setup confirmation, and the real-doctor-to-check gate.

Run in a fresh project environment, without an importable Hermes installation:

```bash
uv sync --extra dev
uv run --extra dev pytest -q
uv run --extra dev ruff check .
uv build
git diff --check main...HEAD
```

Verified on this head after rebasing onto the 0.17.1 release:
- 1699 passed, 40 skipped, 5 xfailed.
- Ruff 0.16.6 passed.
- Source distribution and wheel built successfully.
- Diff whitespace check passed.

## Platforms

- [x] Windows — CPython 3.12.11, fresh project dev environment
- [ ] Linux — pending GitHub CI
- [ ] macOS — not tested locally

## Live receipt

Live Google verification remains pending. No live provider session was opened during implementation. The check-gate regression deliberately stops at an offline transport sentinel and reports failure; it proves the false static blocker is removed, not that Google accepted a credential.

The Gemini transport, session-time credential resolver, and delegation path are unchanged. Before release, obtain a bounded `hermes talk check --provider gemini --no-run --json` receipt on a configured host. The separate Gemini 3.1 text-trigger protocol question is outside this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] One logical change; regression tests included
- [x] Full local suite and pinned Ruff pass
- [x] Conventional Commit with Gemini scope
- [x] Diagnostics remain offline and read-only; no auth-store writes added
- [x] New receipts omit key values; test keys are synthetic
- [x] User-facing messages distinguish configuration from live authentication
- [x] Operating documentation updated
- [x] Changelog entry is under Unreleased, after the 0.17.1 release
- [ ] Independent review of this exact diff
- [ ] Live Gemini verification before release

title: fix(dashboard): make transport stop() idempotent and failure-proof
body:
## What

The dashboard transport's `stop()` is now idempotent and every teardown step is guarded, so a throw in one can never skip the rest.

Previously a throw in `abortCascade()` (or any other teardown step) left the channel and peer open — the server kept listening even though the UI reset to idle, and a second `stop()` could throw again. Each step now nulls its own reference and swallows its own failure, so teardown always completes and a repeated call is a no-op.

## Why

Found while building a standalone mobile surface that reuses the dashboard transport (`dashboard/plugin_api.py` + the lifted `TalkTransport`). Hitting End/New Session could strand the session: the UI reset to idle but the server kept listening, so the next session started with the previous one still live.

## Test

New regression test in `tests/test_dashboard_js.py` drives the real bundle through `node` with a throwing `abortCascade()` and asserts every wire (channel, peer, mic track, audio element) is closed and nulled. Verified it fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

```
pytest tests/test_dashboard_js.py -q   # 6 passed
```

## Changelog

Entry added under `[Unreleased] → Fixed`.

title: feat: GPT-Live voice mode (client delegation) behind TALK_VOICE_MODE=live
body:
## What

Adds an opt-in **GPT-Live** voice mode to the talk plugin's realtime transport, gated behind `TALK_VOICE_MODE=live` (default remains the existing Realtime path, fully untouched).

GPT-Live is OpenAI's Realtime successor — native listen-while-speaking full duplex, and it **delegates** tool/reasoning work to a backend lane instead of running one model for everything. This maps well onto the plugin's existing task architecture, so the live lane dispatches delegation through the **bound task controller** (`connection_id` + `generation` auto-injected) rather than legacy process-wide `/runs`.

## Changes

- **`talk_wire.py`** — `mint_live_session()` relays the client SDP to `POST /v1/live/sessions` (credential stays server-side, provider error bodies redacted); honors `voice` end-to-end.
- **`talk_config.py`** — `TALK_VOICE_MODE=live` added to `TALK_VOICE_MODES`; `LIVE_TALK_MODEL` names the live voice model, fail-closed on empty/unknown.
- **`dashboard/plugin_api.py`** — `/session` accepts `sdp` in live mode (400 if missing); refuses `codex-oauth` in live mode with an explicit remediation instead of silently falling back.
- **`dashboard/dist/index.js`** — live dial via `apiCall` (carries dashboard session auth + `x-talk-token`), `session.*` event set, delegation through `this.task.request("/tool", …)` bound to the selected connection/generation, delegation claimed once by ID (duplicate events do not double-dispatch; changed payloads under the same ID refuse), transcript deltas kept as timestamped fragments rather than synthesized turns.
- **Docs** — README (GPT-Live documented; the old "no developer API" claim removed), `docs/OPERATING.md`, `CHANGELOG`.

## Test coverage

- Focused Python suite: **247 passed** (config, wire, auth, cascade voice, dashboard API, dashboard JS).
- JS dashboard suite: **41 passed** (includes the live-delegation transport, dedup, and transcript-fragment tests).
- `ruff check .`: clean.
- Full suite on this head: 1957 passed, 12 failed — all 12 are pre-existing environment failures on `main` (api-server-vs-in-process capability tiering, and a `TALK_VOICE` env leak in the cascade test), unrelated to this PR.

## Notes for reviewers

- The live mint uses a **project** API key (Realtime accepts a Codex OAuth token; GPT-Live rejects OAuth — documented in OPERATING.md). Live mode requires a real project key; it does not silently fall back to Codex OAuth.
- Realtime path is byte-for-byte unchanged; flip-back is `TALK_VOICE_MODE=native` + restart.
- The fork history was rebased to drop a local loopback-auth carve-out so this PR contains only the GPT-Live work.

## CI

The one red run on the current head was **not** a regression here. It was a pre-existing Windows-only flake in `tests/test_codex_worker.py::test_current_approval_once_and_replay_cannot_authorize_a_new_request` — that test is byte-identical to `main`, this PR touches no codex-path files, and 4 runs at this exact head gave 3 green / 1 red.

**If you see the Windows jobs (3.12 / 3.13) fail with a `PermissionError` on `peer.json`, that is this flake, and it is fixed in #139** — which removes the shared-file race by construction rather than retrying it, and touches no production code. Once #139 lands, this matrix is deterministic.

title: fix(worker): remove the peer.json race and bound the wedged-peer CI hang
body:
Two independent Windows-only CI problems in the codex path. Both are fixed at the root — no retries, no timing windows, no test-only band-aids.

## 1. The `peer.json` race (`fix(tests)`)

`test_current_approval_once_and_replay_cannot_authorize_a_new_request` (and the other `peer()` consumers) intermittently failed on **windows-latest** only:

```
PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: ...\test_current_approval_once_and0\peer.json
```

**Root cause.** The fixture and the test shared *one mutable file*. `save()` wrote a `.tmp` and called `os.replace()` onto `peer.json` while the test's `peer()` had that same path open for read. On POSIX you may replace an open file; on Windows an open handle blocks the replace, so whichever side ran second raised `PermissionError`. Retrying cannot remove that race, only hide it.

**Fix, by construction.** `save()` now writes each snapshot to its own never-reused name (`peer-00000001.json`, `peer-00000002.json`, …). A reader only ever opens a fully written file, and a writer never collides with a read in flight. The fixture loads the newest snapshot at startup, preserving the cross-restart accumulation (`processes`, `requests`, `approval_replies`) the tests assert on. `peer()` reads the newest snapshot; the three "no process started" checks become `peer_wrote_nothing()`.

## 2. A wedged peer could hang a job forever (`fix(worker)`)

While diagnosing the flake above, a **second, worse** problem surfaced: `windows-latest, 3.12` sat in the **Test** step for **51+ minutes** while its Windows siblings finished in ~4, and an earlier run reached **3445 minutes**. That is not a slow test — it is a hang, and nothing stopped it.

**Root cause.** `CodexWorker.run()`'s event loop had a *cancel* deadline but **no overall deadline**, so a live-but-silent app-server peer left it spinning indefinitely. The tests ran the worker inside `ThreadPoolExecutor`, whose exit path calls `shutdown(wait=True)` with no timeout — so one wedged worker thread held the entire pytest process open forever. Reproduced on Linux:

```
inside with-block, exiting now...
exit=124 (TIMED OUT => hung forever)
```

**Fix.**
- **Worker:** added `PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S = 300.0`. If no state-changing event arrives within that window the turn fails closed with `outcome_unknown` — the existing code that already maps to state `unknown`. A silent peer now terminates instead of spinning.
- **Tests:** the three `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...)` blocks now use a `run_worker()` helper — a daemon thread with a bounded join — so a stuck worker fails the test loudly instead of hanging the process.
- **CI:** `timeout-minutes: 15` on the `test` job (healthy jobs are ~3–4 min, so ~5x headroom). Without a ceiling a wedge occupies a runner until GitHub's 6-hour default.

## Verification

- **CI green on `3b9568a`** — all 6 matrix jobs pass; Windows max **4.3 min** (ubuntu ~1.4 min, windows 3.4–4.3 min).
- **Both guards proven with real output:**
  - bounded join: infinite hang → `AssertionError` in 10.2s
  - progress deadline: silent peer → `state='unknown', error='outcome_unknown'` in 1.2s
- **No regressions:** full suite **1945 passed, 57 skipped, 5 xfailed, 12 failed**; the same 12 fail with these changes stashed (all pre-existing environment failures in `test_capabilities` / `test_dashboard_cascade`, none in the codex path).
- `ruff check .` → clean.

## Caveat

The **specific** test that hangs on Windows is still unidentified — the hang does not reproduce on Linux (suite completes in ~104s) and the live job's logs returned `BlobNotFound`. This fixes the proven *mechanism*, not a line observed hanging. If a wedge recurs, `PROGRESS_TIMEOUT_S` and the bounded join will now name the test instead of hiding it.

## Commits

- `8a083b3` — `fix(tests): remove the peer.json race instead of retrying it`
- `3b9568a` — `fix(worker): bound the no-progress wait so a wedged peer cannot hang CI`

title: feat: GPT-Live subscription/API voice and Codex task workers
body:
Connect GPT-Live voice to a selected Hermes task on dashboard, terminal and Discord, with explicit subscription or API authentication and background Codex workers. Subscription is the default and never falls back to paid API. Task ownership and action receipts connect input, delegation, same-job steering, approvals, results and reconnects while conversation continues.

Includes native and browser transports, shared task controls, Discord operator/audience guards, startup cancellation, worker liveness fixes, packaging and operating instructions. Requires the compatible host changes in https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-agent/pull/9 and Codex CLI 0.154.0 for the optional worker.

Validation:
- Automated Talk regression: 2,231 passed, 48 skipped, 5 expected failures. Final Discord startup-control regressions: 152 passed, 3 skipped.
- Real GPT-Live connection smoke checks passed for subscription through aiortc and API through aiohttp.
- Source distribution and wheel builds passed; installed imports resolve to the updated host and plugin.
- Installed host 0.21.1 and Talk 0.18.0 candidate restarted successfully. Gateway and dashboard ports are listening, and Discord and the API server report connected.

Signed-off-by: SmokeDev <degensmoke@gmail.com>

title: feat(talk): repair Live responsiveness and verified recipient routing
body:
## What changes

Live delegation can spend seconds deciding where work belongs. Previously that decision blocked transcript, status and control requests, and a message intended for an existing app could be confused with starting a worker. This release keeps those requests moving and separates the addressed application task from the Hermes conversation that owns voice permissions.

- Persist async delegation admission and exact transcript event identities, with bounded batching and durable native reconnect capture.
- Keep progress and completion tied to the original operation, independently of transcript persistence and interrupted audio.
- Add host-verified recipient listing, selection, delivery reconciliation and on-demand inspection. Selected Talk-owned Codex workers use the existing canonical same-job steering path; they are never silently substituted for Desktop tasks.
- Preserve subscription as Talk's default and require explicit API billing. Discord audience authorization and remote-host ownership remain current on control and private output.
- Package the new modules, update operating documentation, and prepare version 0.19.0.

## Verification

Targeted browser/protocol/presentation regressions: 157 passed, including a real 25-second routing delay and completion eligible in 78 ms while persistence was blocked. Native switch/CLI cases: 23 passed. Gemini/routes: 99 passed. Recipient/dashboard integration: 95 passed. Transcript recovery: 34 passed. Worker recipient manager-level test proves one steering delivery across lost acknowledgment, duplicate call and changed selection.

Ruff and diff checks pass. The release package contains all 69 declared modules; their bytes match the source, wheel, sdist and clean offline installation. Both notice files, 13 changed imports and durable capture/transcript recovery checks pass. The final Linux/Windows CI matrix runs on this PR.

Four real provider connection checks passed: subscription and API on native and browser transports, with each owned session closed. The installed Codex worker returned the exact requested response using the configured model. These checks are distinct from operator microphone acceptance. Existing-app posting is verified by its own recipient receipt; discovering a window or writing a peer socket does not establish delivery.

Signed-off-by: SmokeDev <degensmoke@gmail.com>

title: feat(desktop): plug-and-play Talk in the current conversation
body:
Hermes Talk now opens on the conversation already selected in Desktop. Click Talk, then Connect: a small nonmodal popover dismisses when connected, while status and Stop remain beside the composer. Reopening the controls preserves the same call, captions and background results. Dismissing during connection keeps that request alive; failures reopen actionable controls. Explicit Stop, owner changes and microphone-lease loss still clean up the transport.

The native path uses the Desktop-owned backend's private authentication bridge, with no renderer token field or stored credential. Connect prepares the exact current conversation, including a new empty chat, before requesting audio. Missing, stale or ambiguous targets never fall back to another conversation or legacy unbound mode. Browser dashboard authentication remains unchanged, subscription remains the default, and paid API use stays explicit.

The shared Live/Realtime transports and durable coordinator are reused. Companion host: TheSmokeDev/hermes-agent#12. Requirements and operating instructions are in docs/DESKTOP.md; the compatible host is required.

Packaged Desktop Start, Switch and Return omit browser-page metadata because the Electron file URL is not a webpage. This fixes the reported 400 invalid_event rejection without changing the backend URL guard. HTTP/HTTPS dashboards retain their page references. Non-authentication failures offer Try again instead of incorrectly instructing the operator to reconnect.

Validation: 107 targeted Desktop, dashboard and generated-UI regressions pass, with lint and generated-bundle checks. Eight independent real React/Radix scenarios pass against the final bundle: dismissal and dashboard interaction, reopening without duplicate audio/session creation, Stop, failure/retry, pending connection, owner changes, blank conversation preparation and the real Python file-reference validator. Provider, REST and microphone boundaries in those lifecycle tests are offline doubles. Earlier backend/auth/catalog checks passed. The companion host's required CI checks pass; current Talk head CI is running. The preceding Talk head passed five OS/Python jobs and failed two existing worker timeout tests on Windows Python 3.13; those files are unchanged by this PR.

Installed candidate f3c0db1 matches the generated bundle and retains host c53098f6d0. Credentials, the host's modified lockfile and rollback are preserved. The actual installed UI verifies both Talk entry points, the small popover with no dimming overlay, outside dismissal and reopening on the same conversation; Connect is left ready. The earlier Start rejection was reproduced against the actual local backend: a file-page reference returned 400, omitting it returned 200 for the exact subscription session, and cleanup returned 200. This PR does not claim a new Desktop microphone acceptance result.

SmokeDev

title: auth: Codex lane never rewrites ~/.codex/auth.json; borrows Hermes' Codex login first
body:
Follow-up to the catalog review on NousResearch/hermes-agent#108798: the one blocker for listing `hermes-talk` was that the Codex lane refreshes the OAuth token and rewrites `~/.codex/auth.json`. This makes that lane read-only and lets Talk borrow Hermes' own Codex login first.

- `_resolve_codex_oauth` → `_resolve_hermes_codex_oauth()` first (`hermes_cli.auth_codex.resolve_codex_runtime_credentials`, Hermes owns that store and refreshes under its lock), then `~/.codex/auth.json` **read-only**. Expired CLI token → `TalkAuthError` pointing at `codex login` / `hermes auth login openai-codex`.
- Removed `_post_token_form`, `_write_auth_json`, `_refresh_codex_credential` (+ httpx/tempfile imports). 70 insertions / 204 deletions.
- Tests rewritten to the new contract (store byte-identical after an expired token; Hermes login wins; gemini diagnostics guard patches `httpx` directly). README paragraph updated.

Verified: `tests/test_auth.py tests/test_doctor.py tests/test_core_provider.py tests/test_gemini_diagnostics.py` 117 passed; E2E with real Hermes imports: seeded `$HERMES_HOME/auth.json` → `source=codex-oauth, detail="Hermes Codex login"` with `~/.codex` never created; no Hermes login + expired CLI token → refused, file unchanged.

Once this is in a release, bump the SHA in #108798 and it's ready to merge into the catalog.

title: Subscription resolver misses nested chatgpt_account_id in Hermes-owned Codex JWT
body:
## Summary

In hermes-talk 0.19.1, GPT-Live subscription authentication fails when the plugin borrows a valid Hermes-owned Codex OAuth token.

## Observed behavior

`_resolve_hermes_codex_oauth()` constructs `TalkAuth(..., account_id=None)` and `_resolve_codex_oauth()` returns that credential before checking the Codex CLI store. Subscription validation then rejects the credential because it requires an account ID.

The access JWT contains the existing account identity under the nested claim:

```text
https://api.openai.com/auth.chatgpt_account_id
```

The separate Codex CLI credential store contains the same account identity, and forcing the CLI-store fallback succeeds.

## Expected behavior

When Hermes-owned Codex OAuth is selected, extract the existing nested `chatgpt_account_id` claim and pass it through the current subscription-auth validation/header path. Preserve fail-closed behavior and do not fall back to API billing.

## Scope

- hermes-talk 0.19.1
- affected function: `_resolve_hermes_codex_oauth()` in `talk_auth.py`
- no credentials or private infrastructure details included

title: fix(auth): carry the ChatGPT account id through the Hermes Codex login
body:
Fixes #149.

On a stock Hermes install signed in with `hermes auth login openai-codex`, GPT-Live subscription mode failed in 0.19.1: the borrowed Hermes token came back with no account id and `validate_live_auth` refused it, fail-closed. Only users who had also run `codex login` were unaffected.

The account id lives inside the access token under `https://api.openai.com/auth` → `chatgpt_account_id`, the same claim Hermes reads for its own `ChatGPT-Account-Id` header. This reads it there.

- `_decode_jwt_chatgpt_account_id()` next to the existing JWT helpers
- Hermes path sets `account_id` and `expires_at` from the token; a malformed token yields to the CLI store as before
- CLI store path uses the claim only when `auth.json` has no `account_id`
- No change to fail-closed behavior: no claim → subscription still refused, never API billing

Tests: four new cases run the real `_resolve_hermes_codex_oauth` against a stand-in `hermes_cli.auth_codex` (the existing test monkeypatched the function away, which is how this slipped past CI). Three of them fail on `main` today. Full suite 2382 passed locally.

Signed-off-by: SmokeDev <degensmoke@gmail.com>

title: feat: OpenAI-compatible cascade TTS backend (self-hosted / LiteLLM gateways)
body:
## Problem

`TALK_CASCADE_TTS` is fail-closed to `elevenlabs` only (`TALK_CASCADE_TTS_PROVIDERS = ("elevenlabs",)` in `talk_config.py`). Cascade mode's actual design (per the code comments in `talk_cascade_voice.py`) is already provider-agnostic: the relay/barge-in/error-degradation/playback-sink logic never assumes ElevenLabs specifically, only the WS stream-input wire format and `xi-api-key` header do.

Several self-hosted / gateway TTS options speak an **OpenAI-compatible `POST /v1/audio/speech`** endpoint (LiteLLM proxying a custom TTS model, e.g. `sopro`, Qwen3-TTS via a gateway, etc.). There is currently no way to point cascade mode at one of these without forking the plugin.

## Proposal

Add a second `TALK_CASCADE_TTS` value: `openai` (or `openai_compatible`), backed by the standard OpenAI TTS REST contract:

```
POST {base_url}/audio/speech
{"model": ..., "voice": ..., "input": "<sentence chunk>", "response_format": "pcm" or "wav"}
```

New knobs, mirroring the existing `TALK_ELEVENLABS_*` pattern:
- `TALK_CASCADE_OPENAI_BASE_URL` (required; e.g. a LiteLLM gateway URL)
- `TALK_CASCADE_OPENAI_API_KEY` / falls back to `TALK_OPENAI_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` (set-but-blank refuses, same pattern as every other Talk key)
- `TALK_CASCADE_OPENAI_MODEL` (required — the backend TTS model, e.g. a self-hosted model id)
- `TALK_CASCADE_OPENAI_VOICE` (required — backend-defined voice/speaker id)

## Why REST, not WS stream-input

The OpenAI TTS contract is request/response (one call = one complete audio clip), not a stream-input socket like ElevenLabs'. This fits the existing `SentenceChunker` output naturally: **one REST call per chunk**, decode the response body (WAV or raw PCM per `response_format`), feed PCM straight into the same `on_audio` sink used today. Barge-in reuses the exact same generation-counter abort pattern — cancel the in-flight HTTP request, drop decoded-but-unplayed audio.

## Non-goals

- Not replacing ElevenLabs; both providers coexist behind `TALK_CASCADE_TTS`.
- Not adding a generic provider plugin system (yet) — this is one more fail-closed value in the existing enum, same shape as the current single-value list.

## Reference

Architecture research + integration-point writeup available; happy to open a PR for review once the shape is agreed.

title: feat(results): honest result presentation and playback tracking across transports
body:
Result presentation that never claims more than it can prove. Six facts stay separate: result ready, context submitted, playback started, playback finished, interrupted, unknown. A context append or a provider "response complete" is not evidence of speaker output.

- `presentation` on `/state` events and jobs; `/speech` protocol 1 with measured timing, `playback_supported`, `replay`; `/speech/receipt` with eight states behind a dispatch fence (`submitting` persists before the provider is touched).
- `task_event_speech` extended in place (`protocol`, `claim_expires`, `retry_at`, `retry_count`, `attempt_order`, `response_id`, `facts`); no second ledger.
- Cascade PCM tracks local playback start and drain; browser WebRTC and GPT-Live stay `unknown`; Live declares `playback_supported:false`.
- Native terminal and Discord `/replay EVENT_ID` re-present an existing terminal result; replay never restarts a job or stages input.
- Late receipts for a retired attempt cannot overwrite a newer one.

body:
Three documentation changes. No `.py`, `.js`, workflow or version file is touched.

### `README.md`

The exact string "Hermes Talk" did not appear once in this README. The H1 was the
repo slug, and every other mention was either the slug or the shell command.

- H1 is now the product name.
- The opening paragraph says what the project is — a realtime voice plugin for
  Hermes Agent — before it says where it runs.
- A short **What it is / Who it is for** pair sits near the top, so the scope and
  the non-goals are visible without scrolling.

Badges, the subtitle and every existing section are unchanged.

### `docs/index.html` (new)

A single static landing page, so Settings → Pages can serve the project from
`main` `/docs` with no build step. Plain HTML and CSS, no external scripts or
stylesheets, 9.5 KB, readable in light and dark.

It carries what a repo page cannot: a canonical URL, a meta description, Open
Graph tags, and a schema.org `SoftwareApplication` block naming the project, its
author, its license, its repository and its PyPI download.

Content is install, what it is, the surface table, the provider table and the two
verification commands. Each line matches what `README.md` and the CLI already
say; nothing claims a capability the code does not have.

### `CITATION.cff` (new)

Gives the repo page a "Cite this repository" box and puts the name, author,
license and both URLs somewhere machine-readable.

It deliberately carries no `version` or `date-released`. Those would add a fourth
version surface beside `pyproject.toml`, `plugin.yaml` and
`dashboard/manifest.json`, and it would be the one that silently drifts.

### Checks

```
uv run --extra dev ruff check .                        → All checks passed!
uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/test_repository_hygiene.py → 3 passed
```

### Notes for after merge

- `docs/index.html` only becomes a URL once Pages is enabled (Settings → Pages →
  Deploy from a branch → `main` `/docs`). Until then it is an unreferenced file.
- The repo `homepage` still points at PyPI. It should move to the Pages URL once
  that URL resolves, not before.
- `pyproject.toml` and `plugin.yaml` descriptions also omit the project name, and
  `pyproject.toml` sets no `keywords`. Left alone here on version-file discipline;
  worth folding into the next release bump.

title: feat(input): explicit text input route and Live replay dispatch
body:
The two integration seams the floating panel was waiting on.

**`POST /text/input`** and a `textInput` descriptor on `GET /status`. One authenticated route for explicit operations from the panel: `message` (to the pinned task, or to the exact selected recipient), `start_worker`, `steer`, `cancel`, `approval`. Every call binds `connection_id` + `generation` and fences stale generations; the recipient is the store's current selection compared field for field against the body, never a title; read-only selections are refused; steer/cancel/approval load the owner-scoped action, require `action_id` equality, and re-check run ownership on the live gateway before any POST; a stale approval `request_id` is refused before any POST. The operator's words persist once, then a re-entry guard makes a repeated `input_id` return the stored receipt instead of dispatching twice. Replies carry the honest per-operation state (`queued`, `posted`, `accepted`, `completed`, `failed`, `unknown`, `rejected`, `unsupported`); nothing retries an uncertain dispatch.

**Live replay.** `POST /live/speech` with `replay:true` now revalidates the binding and terminal-result ownership, persists the `submitting` fence, appends the prepared summary into that exact server-owned Live binding, and persists `context_submitted` or `unknown`. It never passes through typed input, the coordinator, or the ledger.

Tests: 28 cases for `/text/input` and 6 for replay, all driving the real ASGI handlers with the real auth gate; 12 of them fail with their guard removed. Full suite locally: 2606 passed.

title: talk check: GPT-Live lane rejects StartResponse after doctor passes
body:
## Summary
`hermes talk doctor` passes the GPT-Live lane, but `hermes talk check` fails before receiving any audio because it sends `StartResponse`, which the GPT-Live client-delegation adapter rejects.

## Environment
- hermes-talk checkout: `a4843d82c0b2c8443830b79f5e0a19b8a78a8303`
- macOS, Hermes CLI, valid Codex OAuth; no API-key fallback.
- `TALK_VOICE_MODE=live`, `TALK_PREFER_CODEX_OAUTH=true`.
- Doctor reports OpenAI, model `gpt-realtime-2.1`, voice `cedar`.
- Local diagnostic-only changes: `_cascade_check()` treats live like native; `LIVE_PROVIDERS` includes the pseudo-provider `live`. No transport changes.

## Reproduction
Run `hermes talk doctor`, then `hermes talk check`.

Observed twice:
```
[PASS] static: doctor: 7 pass, 3 warn, 0 fail
[FAIL] provider_session: live session failed: RealtimeSessionError during send turn: StartResponse is not a GPT-Live client-delegation command
receipt: auth=codex-oauth, ready=yes, response=unfinished, audio=0 bytes, transcript=0 chars
[PASS] hermes_run: ... echoed HERMES_TALK_CHECK_OK
Summary: 2 pass, 1 fail, 0 skip
```

## Expected
The check should use a supported live-lane turn/probe, or explicitly report that this diagnostic is unsupported for this lane, rather than reporting general readiness then sending an incompatible command. The doctor should also make clear which effective live model is used instead of reporting the ordinary realtime default if those differ.

This demonstrates a failing diagnostic/provider-turn path, not proof that microphone-driven GPT-Live sessions are universally broken. No real microphone conversation was exercised in these reproductions.

title: fix(check): the GPT-Live lane can pass `hermes talk check`
body:
Fixes #161.

Three stacked defects on the ChatGPT-subscription lane (`TALK_VOICE_MODE=live`), all on current main:

1. `resolve_provider_lane()` returns the lane `live`, which `run_provider_step` refused as "not a live realtime provider" before any session was built. Every user of the lane got a hard FAIL from `hermes talk check` while doctor passed and live conversations worked.
2. Behind that, the probe sent `StartResponse`, which the Live client-delegation protocol has no encoding for (`talk_live_protocol.encode_command` raises).
3. The probe then waited for `ResponseFinished`, which the Live decoder never emits.

Fix: the provider step admits the live lane, sends one speakable message (`AppendLiveContext(kind="message")`, the same command the plugin uses to voice results, valid in both auth modes) and passes on the first audio back, still under the one wall-clock budget. The refusal for mocks and unknown providers is unchanged. Doctor's model check now reports the live model and voice under live mode instead of `TALK_MODEL`, which is what made the reporter distrust the receipt.

Tests (all fail on the previous code): the live lane reaches the session and passes on first audio with no `ResponseFinished`; it times out without audio instead of hanging; the probe encodes for both auth modes while `StartResponse` still raises; doctor reports the live model and refuses a bad `TALK_LIVE_MODEL`. 106 check+doctor tests pass.

Diagnostic only: nothing here changes a live conversation.

title: fix(desktop): "Talk is temporarily unavailable" on every host without hermes_cli.dashboard_task_context
body:
### What happens

On a stock Hermes Desktop build the composer popover never reaches audio. The first click on **Connect** ends in:

> Talk is temporarily unavailable. Try again.

### Why

`startTalk()` binds the focused conversation first (`SDK.prepareTask()` → `POST /api/plugins/hermes-talk/targets`) and that route answers, on any host without the verified dashboard task context:

```
HTTP 503
{"detail":{"code":"context_unavailable","message":"This host lacks verified dashboard task context support."}}
```

`/status` reports the same verdict up front:

```json
"taskContinuity": {"supported": false, "reason": "context_unavailable"}
```

`context_support()` in `talk_dashboard_tasks.py` returns that because the core module is missing:

```
$ python -c "import hermes_cli.dashboard_task_context"
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'hermes_cli.dashboard_task_context'
```

### Why this is not a local misconfiguration

- The helper is not in the public core: `git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep dashboard_task_context` is empty, `git grep resolve_dashboard_task_context` across all refs gives 0 hits, and neither `bb/gui-gateway-attach-wiring` nor `bb/tui-gateway-attach-core` carries it. Core here: `c712f06dcd` (`version = "0.21.3"`, 115 commits behind `origin/main`).
- It is not in Hermes PR #100666 either — the composer voice ownership PR that `docs/DESKTOP.md` names. That PR only touches `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/*` and `src/sdk/index.ts`.
- Plugin side: `7219f2f` (v0.21.0, #168), no newer `main`.

The rest of the lane is healthy on such a host, so the plugin is one binding call away from working:

| step | result |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /status` | 200, `source: codex-oauth`, `model: gpt-realtime-2.1` |
| `POST /targets` | **503 `context_unavailable`** |
| `POST /session` (no task) | 200, Realtime descriptor minted |
| Realtime SDP exchange vs. upstream | reachable (400 `invalid codec` for a dummy SDP) |

### Fix

PR #170: gate the task binding on the host verdict the surface already fetches (`status.taskContinuity.supported !== false`) at the three binding sites, and keep the documented legacy unbound lane as the fallback. Hosts with the helper bind exactly as before.

### Question

Which behaviour do you want for a host without the verified task context — degrade to the unbound lane (as in the PR), or refuse with a message that names the missing host support? `docs/DESKTOP.md` and `docs/dashboard-task-continuity.md` describe the helper as required host support, but no released core ships it, so today every stock Desktop build hits this. If the intent is "refuse", the PR turns into a named precondition instead of a silent fallback.

title: fix(desktop): keep the composer lane usable on stock hosts (popover dismissal, target binding)
body:
Two fixes for the composer (popover) lane, one commit each.

### 1. `fix(desktop): a host focus change must not dismiss the composer popover`

The host moves focus back into the composer whenever the pointer crosses the transcript (`apps/desktop/src/app/chat/composer/focus.ts`), and Radix dismisses a popover on focus-outside by default. The popover therefore closed the moment the pointer left it — contradicting `docs/DESKTOP.md` ("Clicking away or closing the popover keeps audio running"). Both composer popovers now ignore the focus-outside dismissal; outside click and Escape still close them.

### 2. `fix(web): bind a dashboard target only when the host can authorize one`

Fixes #169.

`startTalk()` binds the focused conversation through `SDK.prepareTask()` → `POST /targets` before it ever dials audio. On a host without `hermes_cli.dashboard_task_context` that route answers `503 context_unavailable`, which surfaced as "Talk is temporarily unavailable. Try again." — the lane could never start, even though `/status` reports the verdict up front (`taskContinuity.supported: false`) and the unbound lane works fine on the same host.

The surface is the layer that owns this decision (it already fetches `/status` for the voice mode), so the gate lives there, next to the existing `SDK.prepareTask` checks:

```js
const taskBinding = Boolean(SDK.prepareTask) && status?.taskContinuity?.supported !== false;
```

- host with the helper → binds exactly as before
- host without it → documented legacy unbound lane
- verdict unknown (status not loaded yet) → previous behaviour

Typed input in the owner lane follows the same flag, so it falls back to the legacy transport instead of asking for a target the host cannot authorize. `SDK.prepareTask` stays untouched — the dashboard lane keeps its catalog.

### Proof

- `python3 scripts/build_ui.py --check` → clean
- `python3 -m pytest tests/test_desktop_js.py tests/test_desktop_hud.py tests/test_dashboard_js.py -q` → **132 passed**
- live host without the helper: `POST /targets` → 503 `context_unavailable`; `POST /session` (no task) → 200 with a Realtime descriptor (`gpt-realtime-2.1`, codex-oauth); Realtime SDP exchange against the upstream endpoint answers `400 invalid codec` for a dummy SDP (endpoint reachable)
- popover: the built bundle was instrumented over CDP. Before the fix the trace was `pointerover → blur/focusout → focusin → onOpenChange false` (no pointer movement at all: the popover stayed open for 6 s), after it the popover survives a pointer pass at five positions and still closes on outside click and Escape.

### Note

This keeps Talk usable on stock hosts; it does not implement the verified task context itself. If you would rather refuse with an explicit precondition message, say so and I'll swap the fallback for that.

title: feat(ui): presence bus — window CustomEvents for phase/live/audio/transcript + command listener
body:
## Why

A second desktop plugin wants to draw the live call — a voice-reactive orb, a
caption ribbon, a mirror on a second screen — while hermes-talk stays the only
thing that owns the microphone, the WebRTC session and the audio element.

Today the only ways for another surface to know a call is live are to fork Talk
or to scrape its DOM (`section.ht-hud[data-active]`, `.htd-status`,
`.htd-captions`). Both are brittle: a class rename breaks the consumer, and a
fork breaks the microphone lease. A one-way event on `window` costs Talk nothing
and removes the reason to do either.

The same argument applies in reverse for control: a hardware button or a status
bar that wants to start, stop, mute or sleep the call should call the same
functions Talk's own buttons call, not synthesise clicks on Talk's markup.

## What

One marker-delimited block of 29 lines in `ui/talk-surface.js`, inside
`TalkPage`, immediately after the state hooks. No new dependencies, no new
files, no change to any existing line.

- **Out:** a `useEffect` that dispatches
  `new CustomEvent('hermes-talk:presence', { detail: { phase, live, audioActivity,
  transcript: transcript.slice(-6), muted, sleeping, at } })` on `window` whenever
  any of those six values change. `transcript` is capped at the last six rows so
  the payload stays small.
- **In:** a `useEffect` registering a `hermes-talk:command` listener whose
  `detail.action` is one of `start | stop | mute | unmute | sleep | wake`,
  mapped onto `startTalk()`, `stopTalk()`, `setMuted(true|false)` and
  `setSleeping(true|false)` — the exact functions Talk's own controls call.
  Unknown actions are ignored. The effect returns its `removeEventListener`
  cleanup.
- A `useRef` holds the latest copies of those four functions (refreshed by an
  effect, never during render) so the listener registers once and still calls
  current closures.

```diff
     const [audioActivity, setAudioActivity] = useState({ input: false, output: false });
     const [appearance, updateAppearance] = useState({ skin: "system", animate: false,
       collapseOnConnect: true, hoverExpand: true });
+    // hermes-jarvis presence-bus BEGIN
+    // Optional presence bus: other surfaces can mirror the live call without reading
+    // Talk's DOM. Inert when nothing listens; commands call Talk's own functions.
+    const presenceBusRef = useRef(null);
+    useEffect(() => { presenceBusRef.current = { startTalk, stopTalk, setMuted, setSleeping }; },
+      [startTalk, stopTalk, setMuted, setSleeping]);
+    useEffect(() => {
+      if (typeof window === "undefined") return;
+      try {
+        window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("hermes-talk:presence", { detail: { phase, live,
+          audioActivity, transcript: transcript.slice(-6), muted, sleeping, at: Date.now() } }));
+      } catch (e) { /* the bus is optional */ }
+    }, [phase, live, audioActivity, transcript, muted, sleeping]);
+    useEffect(() => {
+      if (typeof window === "undefined") return undefined;
+      const onCommand = (event) => {
+        const api = presenceBusRef.current || {}, action = event?.detail?.action;
+        const call = (fn, value) => { if (typeof fn === "function") fn(value); };
+        try {
+          if (action === "start") call(api.startTalk);
+          else if (action === "stop") call(api.stopTalk);
+          else if (action === "mute" || action === "unmute") call(api.setMuted, action === "mute");
+          else if (action === "sleep" || action === "wake") call(api.setSleeping, action === "sleep");
+        } catch (e) { /* a command never breaks the call */ }
+      };
+      window.addEventListener("hermes-talk:command", onCommand);
+      return () => window.removeEventListener("hermes-talk:command", onCommand);
+    }, []);
+    // hermes-jarvis presence-bus END
 
     const transportRef = useRef(null);
```

Per `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the regenerated `dashboard/dist/index.js` and
`desktop/plugin.js` are committed alongside the source change
(`python scripts/build_ui.py`).

Event names are namespaced `hermes-talk:*` so they cannot collide with the host
app or another plugin.

## Compatibility

- **No behaviour change when nobody listens.** `dispatchEvent` on an event with
  no listeners is a no-op, and `addEventListener` on `window` adds nothing
  visible. No existing line moves; no existing state or function changes.
- **The payload is a snapshot, not a handle.** Consumers get values, never the
  transport, the audio element or a setter. Nothing in the block reads or writes
  the media stream.
- **Commands only call what Talk already exposes to its own buttons.** There is
  no new capability: anything reachable over the bus is reachable by clicking.
  `startTalk` still enforces its own guards (phase, WebRTC support, an authorized
  task for GPT-Live), so a `start` while a call is running is ignored by Talk
  itself, exactly as a second click would be.
- **Defensive by construction.** Both effects are inert when `window` is
  undefined (SSR, the `vm`-context test harnesses), the dispatch is wrapped in
  `try/catch` so an environment without `CustomEvent` degrades silently, every
  command call is guarded by `typeof fn === 'function'`, and unknown actions fall
  through. No `console` output anywhere in the block.
- **Hook order is stable.** The three hooks are unconditional and sit between the
  state hooks and the refs, so the slot order used by the repo's test harnesses
  stays consistent across renders.
- **Cost.** One extra event per state change that already caused a re-render;
  one `window` listener per mounted `TalkPage`, removed on unmount.

## Test notes

Run against a throwaway copy of the plugin — the reference install was only read.

- `pytest tests/test_ui_build.py tests/test_ui_presentation.py tests/test_dashboard_js.py
  tests/test_desktop_js.py tests/test_desktop_hud.py tests/test_typed_panel.py -q`
  on hermes-talk 0.20.2: **163 passed before the patch, 163 passed after it**
  (same copy, patch applied, bundles regenerated). No test needed changing.
- `python scripts/build_ui.py` regenerates both bundles; `python scripts/build_ui.py --check`
  is clean afterwards. `node --check` passes on `desktop/plugin.js` (copied to
  `.mjs`, since the desktop bundle is ESM) and on `dashboard/dist/index.js`.
- Behavioural proof (hermes-jarvis `tests/test_patch_talk_presence.py`): the
  patched dashboard bundle is rendered in a `vm` context with a fake hooks
  runtime. The first render dispatches a `hermes-talk:presence` event carrying
  exactly `phase, live, audioActivity, transcript, muted, sleeping, at`;
  `mute`/`unmute`/`sleep`/`wake` flip the matching state; `start` moves `phase`
  to `starting` and `stop` back to `idle`; an unknown action changes nothing; the
  listener stays registered exactly once across repeated renders. The same
  harness fails against the unpatched bundle (negative control).
- Reverting restores `ui/talk-surface.js` byte-for-byte, and the rebuilt
  `desktop/plugin.js` and `dashboard/dist/index.js` return to their committed
  bytes.
- Not yet verified: a live call with a real microphone and a real consumer
  attached. That happens on Gabriel's MacBook when the Jarvis overlay ships.

## Revert

```bash
python3 ~/projects/hermes-jarvis/scripts/patch-talk-presence.py \
  --talk <root> --revert
```

The revert is deterministic on its own: the block is marker-delimited, so
removing exactly those lines restores the file. The recorded sha256 is what turns
that into a proof, and there are three outcomes:

- **sidecar present, hashes agree** — the file is written, the sidecar is
  deleted, both bundles rebuild back to their stock bytes. Exit 0.
- **sidecar present, hashes differ** — the file was edited while patched, so the
  script refuses: nothing is written. Exit 4. Restore `ui/talk-surface.js` from
  hermes-talk (or `git checkout --` it on the mini) and re-run.
- **sidecar absent** (deleted, or the block was applied by hand) — the marked
  block is still removed and the bundles still rebuild, but the restore is *not*
  hash-verified. Exit 0 with a notice saying so; run `--check` (expect exit 1)
  and, on the mini, `git diff` to confirm the tree is clean.

Upstream, the equivalent is reverting the single commit: nothing else in the tree
depends on it.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.0 to 4.38.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.38.1

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146
Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.4. #4106

4.37.8 - 21 Aug 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.7 - 13 Aug 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.3. #4085

4.37.6 - 04 Aug 2026

  • Changed the default filepath for the new remote file address format that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 / 3.37.0 to .github/codeql-config.yml to align it with the suggested path that is used elsewhere. #4070

4.37.5 - 03 Aug 2026

  • Fixed a bug where a network error while streaming the download of the CodeQL bundle could terminate the init Action instead of falling back to downloading the bundle before extracting it. #4061

4.37.4 - 29 Jul 2026

  • This version of the CodeQL Action adds support for the tools input for the codeql-action/init step to be specified using a github-codeql-tools repository property. This feature will gradually be rolled out following the release of this version. Once rolled out, this allows for the CodeQL CLI version that is used in GitHub-managed workflows, such as Default Setup, to be set to a custom value. For example, customers who run into issues with rate limits when a new CodeQL CLI version is released can set the value to toolcache to always use the CodeQL CLI version that is available in the runner toolcache. For Advanced Setup workflows, the value provided for tools in the workflow definition always takes precedence unless the value of the repository property starts with !. #4037
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.2. #4051

4.37.3 - 22 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.37.2 - 21 Jul 2026

  • The new address format for the config-file input that was introduced in CodeQL Action 4.37.0 is now enabled by default. In addition to the format described there, the remote= prefix can now be used to explicitly indicate that the input refers to a remote file. All previous input formats continue to be accepted as well. #4023

title: fix(desktop): bind GPT-Live without a preselected task, show why a request failed; release 0.21.1
body:
## What and why

This follows up #170, which is now on `main`, and brings `main` back to green. The fixes come from the #170 review and the Discord reports that Desktop Talk "refuses to connect" with nothing in devtools.

1. **The GPT-Live start check is back the right way round.** #170 changed `!SDK.prepareTask` to `taskBinding`, which inverted it. On a host that has task context, in GPT-Live mode with no task preselected (an empty conversation on the Talk-enabled build, or a catalog that hasn't loaded or has failed), Connect stopped before `prepareTask` and `/session`. The check is now `!taskBinding`. On a host without task context, the panel refuses GPT-Live before connecting, with this message:
   - before: "Choose an authorized task before starting GPT-Live."
   - after: "GPT-Live needs a Hermes host with task context support, which this host does not report. Use OpenAI Realtime here (TALK_VOICE_MODE=native)."
2. **A failed request now shows why.** Desktop plugin requests go over IPC, so the Network tab never shows them, and every 503 used to read as "Talk is temporarily unavailable." Now:
   - The panel adds `Error code: 503 context_unavailable` under the notice.
   - The console logs `[hermes-talk] POST /targets failed: 503 context_unavailable`.
   - Only the status and a validated `detail.code` identifier are shown. The refusal's free text still stays out of the view, as the existing no-leak tests require.
   - On a host without task context, the recipient picker says recipients need that support, instead of "The recipient could not be loaded."
3. **`main` goes green again.**
   - `ruff check .` failed on four E501 lines in #170's test. That test now uses a shared page harness whose hooks memoize like React's, and the harness also covers the GPT-Live cases.
   - `plugin-guard` fails on every run with `No module named 'tools.plugin_guard_context'`, because upstream's scanner gained that module. The workflow now downloads it too.
4. **Docs and credit.**
   - `docs/DESKTOP.md` covers hosts without task context, which is every released core today.
   - It also covers remote connections. I read hermes-agent `apps/desktop`: an SSH connection runs `hermes serve --host 127.0.0.1` on the remote and reaches it through `ssh -L`, so Talk's requests arrive on the remote's loopback. URL connections arrive from a non-loopback address, and stock Desktop drops `pluginToken`, so Talk refuses them.
   - The paragraph that described the Talk credential bridge as universal now scopes it to the Talk-enabled build.
   - The README contributors list credits @HearthCore.
5. **`chore(release): 0.21.1`** adds the changelog entry and bumps the three version files. Pushing a tag is still a separate step.

Fixes #169 (the follow-up part; #170 closed it)

## How to test

```bash
uv run --extra dev python scripts/build_ui.py --check
uv run --extra dev ruff check .
uv run --extra dev pytest -q
```

Expected: the build check is clean, ruff passes, and pytest gives `2726 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed`, which is what I got locally.

To reproduce on `main`, check out `origin/main -- dashboard/dist/index.js` and run the new start tests:

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/test_dashboard_js.py -k "task_continuity_false or live_start"
```

On `main`, `test_live_start_binds_its_own_target_without_a_preselected_task` and `test_live_start_on_a_host_without_task_context_names_the_missing_support` fail: `prepareTask` is never called and the refusal message is missing. On this branch all three pass.

I also ran the plugin guard against the pinned upstream scanner (with `plugin_guard_context.py`). It reported `verdict safe, zero critical/high findings`.

## Platforms

- [ ] Windows
- [x] Linux
- [ ] macOS

Linux only locally; CI covers ubuntu and windows on Python 3.11–3.13. Nothing here was run on a real Desktop build, and SSH end to end is untested.

## Live receipt

Not applicable. No provider lane, credential resolution or delegation path changes. The changes are the client-side start check, error presentation and docs.

- [x] `pytest -q` and `ruff check .` pass locally on the pinned ruff
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits with a hermes-talk scope
- [x] No auth-store writes outside the documented Codex refresh; tokens reach only the provider's own host
- [x] Nothing secret in logs, receipts, spoken sentences, or test fixtures (the console line carries route and code only)
- [x] Every spoken sentence I added or changed claims only what an artifact proves (none are spoken; the panel text is quoted above)
- [x] Docs updated where behaviour changed (`docs/DESKTOP.md`, README contributors)
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` entry added, under `[0.21.1]`, matching how #168 shipped its version entry

title: test(relay): make the never-started timeout test deterministic
body:
## What and why

`ci` on `main` is red at aad0680 (the #173 merge). Only `test (windows-latest, 3.11)` failed:

```
FAILED tests/test_relay.py::test_pending_tool_timeout_says_it_never_started - assert 'did not start' in "The second tool is still running after 0.02 seconds. ..."
```

#173 isn't the cause; it only changed CodeQL action pins. The test was racy:
- It waited a fixed 5 ms for the first relay call to reach the pool's only worker.
- Both calls share the same 0.02 s wait.
- When the worker thread was slow to be scheduled, the first call timed out and was cancelled before it ever started.
- The worker then picked up the second call, which correctly reported "still running", not "did not start".

The test now occupies the worker with a job submitted straight to the pool and waits on that job's `started` event before sending the call under test. It checks the same behaviour: a call queued behind a busy worker says it never started. It just no longer depends on thread scheduling. There are no product code changes.

## How to test

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest -q tests/test_relay.py
uv run --extra dev ruff check .
uv run --extra dev pytest -q
```

To reproduce: I delayed the worker thread's start by 21–24 ms, which puts it inside the window between the two timeouts. With that delay the old test fails with exactly the CI message, and the new test passes at every delay from 0 to 60 ms. The new test also passed 300 repeated runs with no delay. Full suite: `2726 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed`; ruff is clean.

## Platforms

- [ ] Windows
- [x] Linux
- [ ] macOS

Linux only locally; CI covers ubuntu and windows on Python 3.11–3.13.

The operator ID is correct in TALK_DISCORD_OPERATOR_USER_IDS and the SSRC mapping resolves.

Root cause (verified with a temporary log in the response.created parser of talk_grok_realtime.py):
  response.created keys = ['id','object','output','status','status_details','usage']
  response.metadata     = absent (meta_keys = [])
The plugin sends the binding token in response.create metadata (talk_grok_realtime.py StartResponse -> "metadata";
talk_operator_auth.py:625) and expects it back at talk_operator_auth.py:660. xAI's server does not echo it, so the
binding never happens and the gate fails closed. Failing closed is correct; the Grok lane just cannot satisfy it.

Ask: either document that state-changing voice tools are unavailable on the Grok lane, or bind the response by another
mechanism that xAI does return (e.g. correlate on the response.id of the response the plugin itself created).
Happy to test a patch.

title: Install blocked: hermes-agent:dev ruff==0.15.10 vs hermes-talk[dev] ruff==0.16.7 conflict, reproducible after full update
body:
### Summary
`hermes plugins enable hermes-talk` (and `install ... --enable`) fails with a `DependencyConflict` on a fully up-to-date, git-installed Hermes core. Confirmed this is **not** a version-lag issue: reproduced identically before and after `hermes update` moved core from commit `e9d7a18d` to `bd0affe5` (12 commits, "Up to date" afterward).

### Error
```
hermes_cli.plugins_admission.DependencyConflict: Plugin 'hermes-talk' conflicts with the dependencies pinned by Hermes core or an enabled plugin, so it was not admitted. Resolver: uv lock exited 1: × No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers:
  │ python_full_version == '3.14.*' and sys_platform != 'android'):
  ╰─▶ Because hermes-agent:dev depends on ruff==0.15.10 and hermes-talk[dev]
      depends on ruff==0.16.7, we can conclude that hermes-talk[dev] and
      hermes-agent:dev are incompatible.
```

### Root cause
`hermes-talk`'s actual runtime dependencies are minimal and conflict-free:
```toml
dependencies = ["httpx>=0.27", "aiohttp>=3.9"]
```
but its `dev` extra pins `ruff==0.16.7` (main branch now shows `0.16.8`). Hermes core's own `:dev` dependency group pins `ruff==0.15.10` (`pyproject.toml` line ~550, unchanged across the 12-commit update I just tested). When Hermes's plugin admission runs `uv lock` to validate a new plugin, it appears to resolve the **whole workspace including both projects' `dev` extras simultaneously**, so these two unrelated dev-tooling pins collide even though neither is a runtime dependency a normal user would ever need installed.

### Environment
- Windows 11, Hermes installed via git, Python 3.14.7
- Hermes Agent v0.21.5+6224.gbd0affe (confirmed "Up to date" at time of filing)
- hermes-talk pinned sha `981711b8` (catalog), same conflict reproduced against latest `main` pyproject.toml fetched directly from GitHub

### Ask
- From the Hermes side: should plugin admission's dependency resolution exclude `dev`/test-only extras entirely when enabling a plugin for normal (non-contributor) use? A regular user should never need `hermes-talk[dev]`'s lint tooling just to turn the plugin on.
- From hermes-talk's side: is there a reason the `dev` extra needs installing during a normal `plugins enable`, or is this purely a side effect of how Hermes resolves workspace members? Happy to test a fix on either end.

This fully blocks installing hermes-talk on any git-sourced Hermes install where core's dev ruff pin doesn't happen to satisfy whatever hermes-talk's dev extra currently pins — which, given both move independently, seems likely to recur.

title: Gateway /talk join replies with the terminal message on Hermes after #105279 (sync plugin commands run off the event loop)
body:
## Summary

On current Hermes, `/talk join` in Discord never starts a session. The gateway replies with the terminal message:

> Those are for the gateway's Discord voice channel. Here in a terminal, plain `/talk` starts the call; the standalone `hermes talk` command adds Enter to pause and resume the microphone.

Speech then falls through to the host's native `/voice` lane.

## Versions

- hermes-talk 0.21.1 (`981711b8`)
- hermes-agent `068effc346` (2026-10-08, macOS, launchd). The dispatch change is `e794bb31cb` "fix(gateway): run sync plugin command handlers off the event loop" (2026-09-21, NousResearch/hermes-agent#105279).
- Grok provider. `hermes talk doctor`: 7 pass, 0 fail. `hermes talk check`: PASS. Both run in a CLI process, so they do not cover this path.

## Cause

`gateway/run_inbound.py` now awaits coroutine handlers on the loop, but runs **sync** handlers in the gateway thread pool:

```python
if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(plugin_handler):
    result = await plugin_handler(user_args)
else:
    result = await self._run_in_executor_with_context(plugin_handler, user_args)
    if asyncio.iscoroutine(result):
        result = await result
```

`_talk_command` is sync and uses `asyncio.get_running_loop()` to choose between the gateway and the terminal. In the pool thread no loop is running, so it always takes the terminal branch. `start_session()` also needs the running loop.

## Reproduction (no voice needed)

Dispatch the registered handler the way `run_inbound.py` does, with a fake `gateway.run._gateway_runner_ref` whose Discord adapter has empty `_voice_clients` / `_voice_receivers`:

- sync `_talk_command("join")` in the pool: the terminal message above
- the same call awaited on the loop: `I'm not in a voice channel — run the join command first` (the expected gateway answer)

## Local fix we run

Register an async entry. It calls `_talk_command` on the loop when a gateway runs in the process, and off the loop otherwise (terminal semantics):

```python
def _gateway_runner_present() -> bool:
    try:
        from gateway.run import _gateway_runner_ref  # host-only, lazy by design
    except Exception:
        return False
    try:
        return callable(_gateway_runner_ref) and _gateway_runner_ref() is not None
    except Exception:
        return False


async def _talk_command_entry(raw_args: str = "", invocation=None):
    if _gateway_runner_present():
        result = _talk_command(raw_args, invocation)
    else:
        result = await asyncio.to_thread(_talk_command, raw_args, invocation)
    if inspect.isawaitable(result):
        result = await result
    return result
```

and `"handler": _talk_command_entry` in `_register_talk_command`.

Possible caveat (not tested): in an interactive CLI with a running loop, Hermes resolves awaitable command results in a helper thread with a 30 s bound (`hermes_cli.plugins.resolve_plugin_command_result`), so in-chat terminal `/talk` may need its own path. We only use the gateway lane.

title: Multiplexed gateway: /talk cannot find a secondary profile's Discord voice connection or TALK_* settings
body:
Related to #184.

On a multiplexed Hermes gateway (`gateway.multiplex_profiles: true`, now the default), the profile that has hermes-talk installed is often a secondary profile. Two lookups then miss that profile:

1. **Voice connection.** `talk_discord.resolve_voice_bridge()` reads `runner.adapters`. In the multiplexer that map holds only the launch (default) profile's adapters. Secondary profiles' adapters are in `runner._profile_adapters[<profile>]` (`gateway/run.py`). If the default profile has no Discord bot, `/talk join` fails with "the Discord adapter isn't loaded on this gateway". If it has one, the lookup uses the wrong bot. Found by code reading on hermes-agent `068effc346`.
2. **Settings.** The multiplexer never loads a profile's `.env` into `os.environ`; each profile gets a context-local secret scope (`agent/secret_scope.py`). `talk_config` reads `TALK_*` from `os.environ`, so for example `TALK_PROVIDER=grok` in the profile's `.env` is not seen in the gateway. Found by code reading; not tested live.

Workaround we use: `gateway.standalone: true` in the voice profile's `config.yaml`, then `hermes -p <profile> gateway install`, so that profile runs its own gateway. Hermes documents this setting as a temporary shim, so a multiplex-aware lookup would be better: resolve the adapter for the invoking profile, and read settings through Hermes' scoped lookup.

title: fix(discord): route offloaded Talk commands back to the gateway loop
body:
## Summary
- Detect Discord through the host's session-scoped platform when the synchronous `/talk` handler is offloaded to a worker without an event loop.
- Return a coroutine for the gateway to await on its owning loop, preserving the original invocation and awaiting nested canonical control results.
- Keep terminal behavior, older-host fallback, and existing host authorization/audience checks intact. No dependency or Ruff pin changes.

## Why
Hermes gateway dispatches synchronous command handlers through a context-preserving executor, then awaits returned coroutines. A worker has no running event loop, but that does not make it a terminal. Previously Discord join, status, and controls returned terminal guidance; plain `/talk` could enter terminal audio instead.

## Regression coverage
A task-local host contract double and real executor reproduce the gateway dispatch shape without making Hermes a test dependency. Tests assert owner-loop execution for plain Talk, join, status, pause, resume, and leave; nested canonical result awaiting and privacy; live-join authorization refusal; scoped platform precedence; and fallback without the gateway module.

## Verification
- Before the fix: new regression selection **8 failed, 2 passed**.
- Relevant subset (`tests/test_register.py tests/test_discord.py tests/test_native_discord.py`): **162 passed, 3 skipped**.
- Full suite on Python 3.11 with current upstream dev dependencies: **2736 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed**.
- `ruff check .` with upstream-pinned Ruff 0.16.8: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

The full local suite required Node on PATH and a scratch pytest base directory (a macOS temporary path containing `private` trips an existing privacy assertion). Those environment issues required no source changes.

## Caveat
This verifies worker/context/owner-loop routing with scripted room methods, not a live Discord end-to-end audio session. Live Discord acceptance remains unconfirmed.

title: fix(deps): move the ruff pin out of the dev extra so Hermes can enable the plugin
body:
## Summary
- Moves the exact ruff version pin from `hermes-talk[dev]` into a new `requirements-lint.txt`; CI installs it with `pip install -e ".[dev]" -r requirements-lint.txt`. The rule-set pin in `[tool.ruff.lint]` is unchanged, so lint behaves exactly as before (still ruff 0.16.10).
- Adds `test_no_extra_carries_an_exact_pin`, and points the existing pin guard at the new file and CI line.
- Updates CONTRIBUTING, README, the PR template, the orchestrator doc and the CHANGELOG (`Unreleased` → Fixed).

## Why
Hermes admits a plugin by adding it to its own uv workspace and running `uv lock` over every extra of every member. `ruff==0.16.10` in our dev extra must then agree with Hermes core's dev-group `ruff==0.15.10`, so `hermes plugins enable hermes-talk` fails with `DependencyConflict` for every user on current Hermes (#180). Contributor tooling pins should never be in metadata a normal install resolves. Moving ruff into a dependency group would not help: uv locks workspace members' groups too (core's own pin *is* the group `hermes-agent:dev`).

## Verification
- On a fresh Hermes Agent v0.22.2 install (Windows 11, Python 3.14.7): `hermes plugins enable hermes-talk` on `main` → `DependencyConflict: ... hermes-agent:dev depends on ruff==0.15.10 and hermes-talk[dev] depends on ruff==0.16.10`. With this change → dependencies resolve and install, plugin enabled; `hermes talk doctor` 7 pass / 0 fail; `hermes talk check` 3/3 PASS (live provider turn + bounded Hermes run).
- The new guard, run against `main`'s `pyproject.toml`, reports `dev: ruff==0.16.10` (red before, green after).
- `ruff check .` via `requirements-lint.txt` → ruff 0.16.10, all checks passed; `tests/test_repository_hygiene.py` 4 passed.

## Not in this PR
#180's second report (Hermes's plugin security scan returning CAUTION, led by a HIGH hit on `build/lib/talk_auth.py`). `build/` is not tracked in this repo; it appears to come from a local build inside the plugin clone. Tracked separately.

Fixes the dependency-conflict half of #180.

title: fix(grok): bind Discord tool authority by order when xAI does not echo metadata (#178)
body:
## What and why

On the Grok lane in Discord, every state-changing voice tool (`delegate_task` and friends) was denied as an unbound response. The ledger sends a one-shot binding token in `response.create` metadata and binds the response only when `response.created` echoes it back. xAI's `response.created` carries no `metadata` at all (reporter verified the keys), so the binding never happened and the gate failed closed.

The fix keeps the gate fail-closed but gives a non-echoing provider a safe way to bind: the ledger takes an `echoes_response_metadata` flag (false only for Grok, set in `talk_cli`). When it is false, a `response.created` that carries no metadata at all binds to the single outstanding binding. It does not bind when:
- two or more bindings are outstanding (ambiguous),
- the event carries an unknown token or any metadata (a forgery is not a missing echo),
- the provider echoes (OpenAI and Gemini are unchanged).

Automatic responses are already off when the ledger is on, so every response in flight was requested by the plugin.

Fixes #178

## How to test

```bash
uv run --extra dev pytest tests/test_operator_auth.py -q
uv run --extra dev pytest -q
```

Five new tests: order binding authorizes the operator, still denies a non-operator, refuses with two bindings outstanding, refuses a forged token, and never applies to an echoing provider. Two existing test stubs for the ledger constructor now accept keyword arguments. Full suite: 2780 passed, 57 skipped, 5 xfailed. Ruff clean.

## Platforms

- [x] Windows
- [ ] Linux
- [ ] macOS

CI covers ubuntu + windows on Python 3.11 to 3.13.

## Live receipt

Not run live: it needs a Discord voice session on the Grok lane, which this machine does not have. Not tested against real xAI traffic. The reporter on #178 offered to test a patch.

title: test(catalog): isolate installed Hermes registries in catalog tests
body:
## What and why

Fixes #93.

The catalog tests reset the bound context and caches, but an importable Hermes installation still supplies the in-process catalog. The CLI prompt-composition test similarly assumes that disabling the REST lane means there is no host summary.

This is a **test-only fix**:
- Add an explicitly requested `isolated_capability_catalog` fixture that blocks the seven ambient registry modules in `sys.modules`.
- Catalog tests that need an in-process host still install their existing explicit fakes.
- Use the same monkeypatch undo stack as the tests, so overrides restore in reverse order. An initial nested-context version passed the assertions but leaked module state at teardown; the new two-case regression detects that ordering mistake.
- Apply the fixture to the catalog module's cleanup fixture and the single CLI test that expects an absent catalog.
- Invalidate cached/pending catalog writes at fixture boundaries, update the contributor note and changelog.

No production Python, provider adapters, credentials, delegation policy, or live voice behavior changes.

## Verification

Base: `cc8055c314dcb4a1528eedb38c781e53bd78437e`.
Patch: `e02046280e08c242ea11e15198ac0f8a523e8b9d`.

Linux, Python 3.12.14; pytest 9.1.1, pytest-timeout 2.4.0, pinned Ruff 0.16.10.

- Unmodified base, `tests/test_capabilities.py tests/test_cli.py`, no host: **107 passed**.
- Unmodified base with synthetic importable Hermes registries: **13 failed, 94 passed**. The failures were unexpected in-process catalog results / host summary, not a real Hermes installation or network failure.
- Patched target files plus `tests/test_catalog_isolation.py`, synthetic host present and module-restoration checks after each test: **109 passed**.
- Final complete suite: `python -m pytest -p pytest_timeout -q --tb=short --maxfail=10` → **2771 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed**.
- `ruff check .` with 0.16.10 → **All checks passed**.
- `git diff --check` → clean.

Tests ran with an isolated temporary HOME and no inherited credentials. The focused runner blocked socket/subprocess calls; it observed and blocked a background API-probe socket attempt after one run. The complete-suite runner allowed loopback test peers and synthetic subprocesses, while rejecting non-loopback connects and real agent executable names outside temporary fixtures. No paid/model/real microphone session was used. This is self-testing, not independent QA.

The 63 skips and 5 expected failures are not counted as passes. Windows and macOS were not run locally. No live-provider receipt is claimed or required for this test-only change.

## Reproducing the installed-host condition

Before running the two affected test files, install synthetic registry modules into `sys.modules`, using the existing `_install_fake_host` helper in `tests/test_capabilities.py`. For the reported failure set, use a synthetic skill, one non-browser toolset, and no resolved tools; run the tests in that same Python process. On the base, REST/absent-host assertions receive `in-process`; with this patch they remain isolated. The new committed regression separately checks both absent and installed ambient module entries, explicit test overrides, and restoration after teardown.

## Scope / review

Six files: four test files and two related documentation updates. No new dependency. No UI change. Draft for maintainer review; this does not claim acceptance or merge.

title: fix(relay): defer announcements while operator speech is active
body:
## What and why

Addresses #90. Draft: the stale-event policy and live-audio behavior still need maintainer review.

A synthetic `SpeechStarted` followed by a queued announcement reproduces the existing gap: with no model response in flight, the relay/pump sends the announcement without waiting for `SpeechStopped`.

This change:
- Tracks operator speech for neutral events and the legacy speech-start/stop wire events.
- Clears on a matching stop (or an unnamed stop), ignores a late stop for a different named utterance, and resets at a new session.
- Includes operator speech in the announcement poll **and the real send-lock re-check**.
- Keeps tool authorization, normal response/continuation behavior, and provider implementations unchanged.

## Explicit policy tradeoff

A missing stop cannot hold announcements forever. The proposed `OPERATOR_SPEECH_STALE_S = 120.0` is a code constant, not a new environment knob. Duplicate starts for the same active utterance do not renew its deadline.

After 120 seconds without a matching stop, the speech gate fails open; existing model/playback gates still apply. **An unusually long uninterrupted utterance can therefore overlap an update after this bound.** This is recovery from missing events, not silence detection. The existing 30-second starvation warning is separate. The operating guide states this limitation.

The bound is a reviewable proposal, not a claim that 120 seconds is the universally correct setting.

## Tests

Base: `cc8055c314dcb4a1528eedb38c781e53bd78437e`.
Head: `dbda4fd35cc30f05b77759df3a2407d0f85c9da7`.

- Failing-first synthetic regression: on the base, an announcement is sent while the operator is marked as speaking.
- Added neutral/legacy start-stop coverage, delayed foreign stop handling, duplicate-start deadline, unnamed stop/new-session reset, provider-batch release after stop, and deterministic missing-stop expiry with an injected clock.
- Extended the existing real `send_outgoing` lock-race harness with an operator-speech race.
- Final complete suite: `python -m pytest -p pytest_timeout -q --tb=short --maxfail=10` → **2778 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed**.
- Pinned Ruff 0.16.10: `ruff check .` → **All checks passed**.
- `git diff --check` → clean.
- Remote six-file Git blobs match the tested local source.

Linux / Python 3.12.14 only. Tests used synthetic events/audio and isolated HOME; the complete-suite runner allowed loopback peers and fake subprocesses while blocking non-loopback connections and real agent executable names outside temporary fixtures. Skipped/expected-failing tests are not counted as passes.

## Not verified / not changed

No live microphone, Discord, or provider voice session was exercised; no live-provider receipt is claimed. Windows/macOS were not run locally. These are self-tests, not independent QA.

No new dependency, credentials, production configuration, host integration, or permission/authorization change. This branch is independent of #195. Please keep it Draft until the recovery policy and live-behavior evidence meet the project's bar.
