title: Discord: a response's partial last frame is never played, so finished background results are never announced
body:
## What happens

On the Discord lane, after the model finishes a spoken reply, background results (delegate_task runs) are never announced. The run finishes and is claimed for delivery, but the announcement never goes out. The gateway log then shows:

```
[talk] an update has been waiting 30s for a safe opening
```

In practice, the model keeps telling the operator it doesn't have the answer yet while the result is already sitting in the queue. It only gets read out if the operator asks again and the model calls check_work itself.

## Cause

`_RealtimeSource.read()` in `talk_discord.py` only returns full 3,840-byte (20 ms) frames. When a reply's audio doesn't end exactly on a frame boundary, which is most replies, the remainder stays in `_carry` and is never played: each later read finds the queue empty and returns `SILENCE_FRAME`, but keeps the carry.

Since #50, `DiscordAudio.playback_pending` includes `source.carrying`. With that leftover partial frame held, `playback_pending` stays True for the rest of the call, so `speaker_busy()` never clears and `pump_announcements` waits forever.

Seen on 029cced (current main) with the OpenAI Realtime lane and Discord voice on Linux. It happened on every call: three calls on Nov 16, and each one logged the stuck-announcement or "active response in progress" warnings.

## Repro (offline)

```python
import queue, talk_discord as td
q = queue.Queue(); s = td._RealtimeSource(q)
q.put(b"\x01" * 5000)   # one reply's last audio: 1 full frame + 1,160 bytes
s.read(); s.read(); s.read()
print(s.carrying)       # True, forever
```

## Fix

On an underrun, if a partial frame is held, play it padded with silence and clear the carry. The read returns no more silence than the `SILENCE_FRAME` it would have returned anyway, full frames are unchanged, and the "never return b''" rule is kept. There are regression tests for the padded tail and for `playback_pending` releasing once the tail plays; the existing #50 test that asserted the carry is kept on underrun was updated to match.

We fixed it. Would you like us to open a PR for you to review?

title: Fix CI worker teardown and prepare 0.23.1

title: Switch between Claude Code and Codex chats by voice (0.24.0)
body:
## What changes

Say “Switch to my Codex chat and read its last reply.” On a host with an authenticated recipient bridge, Hermes Talk selects the only open chat for that app and reads its latest visible assistant reply. Claude Code works the same way. Give the title when several chats are open.

In GPT-Live, “Ask it to check mobile too” uses the chat selected when Hermes heard the request. If the target changes while Hermes is reasoning, it asks which chat to use. A stored, read-only conversation stays read-only.

## Compatibility

Selecting, reading and sending require the corresponding capabilities on the execution host. The standalone plugin does not add an external terminal or app bridge to stock Hermes; this PR adds a voice shortcut to the existing host controls. The companion host is TheSmokeDev/hermes-agent (PRs 11 and 13, merged). [Host PR 19](https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-agent/pull/19) adds delivery receipts for current Claude Code versions, and [host PR 20](https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-agent/pull/20) supports the current Codex Desktop chat layout. On Windows the host must run as the same user as the chats and outside any sandbox.

## Verification

**Rebased** onto main at `d3fd646` (#243 experimental settings, Ruff 0.17.5). The 0.24.0 changelog section now includes main's previously unreleased entries. On Windows with Python 3.12: 267 recipient, steer, target-switching, live-coordinator and UI-build tests passed, and `ruff check .` passed.

**Live proof, Claude Code: send proven.** Run on 20 November 2026 (times UTC) on the owner's Windows PC.
- Target: a disposable Claude Code 2.1.330 chat named `hermes-242-canary`, started in an empty temp folder. No other chat was selected or written to.
- Talk side: the real `RecipientService` from this branch, through its dashboard tool path.
- Host side: the companion's real `RecipientBridge` and `ClaudeRecipients`, run as the PC user and unsandboxed. Only the HTTP hop between them was in-process; no full gateway process was started.
- No microphone or realtime session was used.

Steps:
1. `select_recipient(app=claude_code, reference="hermes-242-canary", read_last_reply=true)` answered: “Addressing hermes-242-canary (claude_code). The Hermes voice task is unchanged. Its last reply: SAPPHIRE”.
2. At 07:10:54.096 `send_agent_message` sent “Reply with exactly TANGERINE. Do not use tools.” to the frozen identity.
3. At 07:10:54.595 that chat's transcript recorded a user row with `origin.kind = "peer"` carrying the exact text.
4. At 07:10:58.683 the chat answered `TANGERINE`. Talk's `read_recipient_history` read the reply back from the same chat.

With host PR 19 applied, four more follow-ups were each answered in the same chat: `MANGO` (07:21:27), `KIWI` (07:24:15), `PLUM` (07:25:39) and `PEAR` (07:26:26). Talk's reconcile then returned “The message was posted to hermes-242-canary (claude_code).” The send itself returns “uncertain” at first, because Claude writes the row only when its turn starts, about four seconds later on this PC. Talk's existing reconcile path then confirms it. Without PR 19 the receipt never left `unknown`.

**The 17 November failure.** That attempt ran the host inside the Codex Windows sandbox. The Claude peer pipe has Windows' default DACL: write for the owner, SYSTEM and Administrators only. A restricted token can read history, so selection and readback worked, but its `GENERIC_WRITE` open is denied with error 5. Reproduced against the disposable chat: the open succeeded from a normal process and failed under `codex sandbox`, both unelevated and elevated. Host PR 19 now reports this as `claude_pipe_access_denied`. No Talk code change was needed.

**Live proof, Codex Desktop: send proven.** Run on 21 November 2026 (times UTC), Codex Desktop 26.1117.3838.0, with the host from [host PR 20](https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-agent/pull/20).
- Target: a disposable Codex Desktop chat, `01a1fd1f-e654-7622-a033-65c369b57a09`, opened in the app's own New chat with no project. Its first message, "Hermes 242 canary 4c1e. Reply with exactly SAPPHIRE. Do not use tools.", was answered `SAPPHIRE` at 08:01:45. No other chat was selected or written to.
- Same Talk and host setup as the Claude Code run. The host drove the app window through UI Automation, bound to the chat by its copied deeplink. The clipboard was restored after each copy.

Steps:
1. `select_recipient(app=codex_desktop, read_last_reply=true)`, i.e. the app named alone, answered at 08:12:20: "Addressing ChatGPT (codex_desktop). The Hermes voice task is unchanged. Its last visible reply: SAPPHIRE".
2. `send_agent_message` with "Reply with exactly TANGERINE. Do not use tools." was prepared at 08:12:33 and posted at 08:12:47.
3. The Codex history recorded the user message at 08:12:45.440 and the reply `TANGERINE` at 08:12:47.355.
4. Talk's `read_recipient_history` read both back at 08:13:03.

A second run sent `KIWI`: selected at 08:14:22 (last reply TANGERINE), posted at 08:14:54 with a transcript receipt, and read back at 08:15:11. On the final host commit, `PLUM` was posted at 08:35:24 and read back at 08:35:38.

Before host PR 20, Codex 26.1117 was listed with `proven_control: none`. It had renamed the composer, moved the transcript into a `Conversation` group and renamed the deeplink menu item.

A chat started by `codex exec` and opened in the app is listed and selectable, but the host refuses its history by design. It reads history and native receipts only from chats the Desktop app created. Such a chat was available but not used.

## Release

Bump the standalone package and manifests from 0.23.1 to 0.24.0 and document the voice commands. The Hermes community catalog has its own pin. The 0.24.0 draft release is still unpublished. Publishing waits on the owner, and the hosts need PRs 19 and 20.

title: fix: transcript review loop and Gemini Live tool calls (#229, #227)
body:
Fixes #229
Refs #227

Two fixes for bugs reported by @gocoelho. Thank you for the clear reports and the proposed patches.

## #229: the transcript memory review kept re-spawning itself

**What went wrong.** When a call ends, Talk hands each finished transcript to a memory review. Without a live agent or api server, that review is a detached `hermes -z` one-shot. That one-shot is a normal Hermes run, so it loads hermes-talk too, and when it finishes, its own session-end hook sweeps the transcripts again. If the Talk process that started the review had already exited, nothing held the transcript any more. The review's sweep claimed the same transcript and started another review, which did the same thing when it ended. The reporter measured 2,050 reviews in one day.

**The fix.** `flush_agent` starts the one-shot with `TALK_TRANSCRIPT_REVIEW_CHILD=1` added to its environment, and `sweep_transcripts` returns right away in any process that carries that marker. It is the reporter's proposed fix with a different variable name. The marker is set only in the child's environment, never in the parent's.

**What is unchanged.** A normal session still sweeps as before. A transcript that an exited Talk process left claimed is still reviewed once more by the next normal sweep, the limit the reporter already described. That means one extra review, not a chain. The api-server and live-agent lanes do not start a child process from Talk. Their reviews run inside a long-lived process, and a sweep there keeps the transcript claimed while its review runs. So those lanes can cause at most one extra review, not a chain. They were checked by reading the code, not run live.

**Test.** `test_detached_review_child_cannot_reclaim_an_abandoned_transcript` leaves a transcript claimed by a dead process, runs `flush_agent`'s one-shot tier, and runs a sweep inside the fake child with the child's environment. It checks four things:
- the child does not re-claim the transcript;
- the parent's environment is passed through;
- the marker does not leak into the parent;
- the next normal sweep still reviews the transcript once.

It fails if either half of the fix is removed (checked separately for each half).

## #227: Gemini Live closed with 1007 when a tool schema used `additionalProperties`

**What went wrong.** Talk sent Gemini tool schemas in the function declaration's `parameters` field, which takes Google's OpenAPI-style schema subset. That subset has no `additionalProperties`, so any tool schema using it made the Live API reject the whole setup message with close code 1007 (`Unknown name "additionalProperties"`). Talk's own voice tools in `talk_tools.py` also declare `additionalProperties: false`.

**The fix.** Function declarations now send the tool's JSON Schema unchanged in `parametersJsonSchema`, the declaration field that takes standard JSON Schema and supports `additionalProperties`. Closed objects and nested object rules are kept rather than dropped. The old helper that uppercased `type` names for `parameters` is no longer needed and is removed, and the module docstring now describes the new wire shape. This differs from the reporter's patch, which removes `additionalProperties` from the schema; see the note at the end.

**Test.** `test_live_tools_keep_closed_and_nested_json_schemas` checks that a closed schema with nested `additionalProperties` (and a property literally named `additionalProperties`) reaches the setup message unchanged. The existing setup-message test now expects `parametersJsonSchema`. Both fail on current `main`.

## Test-only commit: the Windows force-kill lease test

In a Windows venv, `sys.executable` is a launcher that starts the real interpreter as a second process. `test_other_process_skips_live_capture_then_recovers_it_after_force_kill` killed and waited for the launcher only. The real interpreter could still hold the transcript lease when the next sweep ran.

The test passes alone but fails under load. With 12 copies running at once:
- on `main`, it failed in 3 of 12 runs;
- on this branch before the change, it failed in 12 of 24 runs;
- after the change, it failed in 0 of 24 runs.

On Windows the child now runs on `sys._base_executable`. CI's `setup-python` interpreter is not a venv launcher, so CI is unaffected.

## Verification

- #229 was reproduced locally. The fix was checked through a real Hermes `hermes -z` one-shot driven by a local model fixture, before this branch was rebased onto current `main`.
- `pytest tests/test_transcript.py tests/test_gemini_realtime.py`: 118 passed, 3 skipped (the skips are symlink tests on Windows).
- `ruff check .` (ruff 0.17.5): all checks passed.
- The full suite ran once locally on Windows 11 with Python 3.12 in a venv, before the test-only commit: 3077 passed, 57 skipped, 5 xfailed, 5 failed. None of the failures involve the changed code, and all five also fail on current `main`:
  - Four are the known Windows timing flakes in `test_codex_cancel_timeout.py` and `test_codex_worker.py`. Two of them, `test_unanswered_probe_bounds_both_local_deadline_and_rpc_waiter[0.25-1.0]` and `test_cancellation_keeps_its_deadline_when_probe_and_interrupt_are_unanswered`, also fail when run alone, on both `main` and this branch. The other two pass when run alone on both.
  - The fifth is `test_other_process_skips_live_capture_then_recovers_it_after_force_kill`, fixed by the test-only commit above.
- No live Gemini or other paid provider calls were made for this PR.

## Not yet verified: #227 on the live API

On Gemini Live, the old setup message reproduced the 1007 close. With this patch, the session got past that point but stopped at the provider's billing check. **A real Gemini Live tool-call round trip with `parametersJsonSchema` has not been confirmed.** That is why this PR says "Refs #227" rather than "Fixes".

The reporter's patch, which removes `additionalProperties`, was confirmed working live by the reporter on v0.22.0, but it drops the closed-object rules. If a live check shows that the Live API does not accept `parametersJsonSchema` for `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`, that patch is the fallback.

title: fix: profile isolation for multiplexed gateways, workers and discovery (#216, #220, #204)
body:
## What and why

Three outside-contributor fixes for one problem: on a multiplexed Hermes gateway (one process serving several profiles), Talk could act for the wrong profile. They touch the same profile context, so they land together on current `main` with authorship preserved.

**1. Settings, keys and Discord bot follow the turn's profile (#216, @Akm0d).** Talk settings and API keys read through `talk_config` now go through Hermes's profile secret scope (`agent.secret_scope.get_secret`) instead of `os.environ`. When Hermes is not importable (standalone, tests) it reads `os.environ` as before. On a multiplexed gateway a read with no profile bound fails closed instead of borrowing the process environment. Discord voice picks the turn's own profile bot from `runner._profile_adapters`; a profile without a Discord bot is refused instead of speaking through the default bot.

**2. Background work keeps the caller's profile (#220, @tancou).** Host and run workers, transcript handoffs, approval workers, SSE readers and timeout timers, and the API/catalog refresh threads capture `contextvars.copy_context()` when dispatched. Work that outlives a turn still runs as the profile that started it. The test-worker cleanup part of #220 already shipped in 0.23.1 (#240), so only the production change, its tests and docs are here.

**3. Catalog discovery is bounded and kept per profile (#204, Kiven / @abaichuan1017).** In-process capability-catalog discovery waits at most `TALK_API_SERVER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S`, so a stuck registry no longer pins the caller, and a stuck read is shared instead of piling up workers.

### Maintainer follow-ups on top (SmokeDev commits)

- **#204 review points** (https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-talk/pull/204#issuecomment-6679268624):
  - Profile context: the reader goes through `_spawn_daemon`, which now copies the caller's context (from #220). A test asserts each read sees its caller's profile home.
  - One pending read per profile: reads are keyed by the resolved Hermes home, so one profile's stuck read never blocks or answers another.
  - Late result kept: a read that finishes after every caller timed out answers the next probe of that profile once (if younger than `TALK_CAPABILITY_CATALOG_TTL_S`), and that probe starts the following read. A host that is always slower than the budget still reaches the in-process tier.
- **Remaining `talk_config`-family reads moved to the scope.** These still read `os.environ`: the language knobs and call-journal switches (added to `main` after #216 branched), the numeric float knobs (`_positive_float`, `talk_audio._env_float`), and doctor's shared-key presence (which would otherwise disagree with the resolver).
- **#216's tests run anywhere.** The `UnscopedSecretError` test depended on a hard-coded path on one machine and was skipped everywhere else. The "multiplex" profile test asserted the standalone result. Both now use a fake `agent.secret_scope` and `gateway.session_context`. Removed `importlib.reload(talk_config)`, `sys.modules.clear()` and the unrestored env pops.
- **Discord guard on host threads.** #216 moved the operator-id read into the profile scope. The native room guard runs per frame on the host's player and receiver threads, which have no profile context. On a multiplexed gateway that read raised there, the guard took it as "revoked", and playback went silent. The guard now reads through a copy of the binding turn's context, and live revocation still works.
- `talk_native_api` uses the package-relative `talk_config` import that its sibling modules use.
- **Catalog probe hardening.**
  - A reader killed by a `BaseException` still resolves its read.
  - A read is registered only after its worker starts.
  - The budget and TTL reads cannot make the probe raise.
- Changelog `[Unreleased]` credits and doc updates (`docs/OPERATING.md`, `docs/BACKGROUND-WORK.md`).

## How to test

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]" -r requirements-lint.txt
pytest -q tests/test_profile_isolation.py tests/test_catalog_probe_timeout.py tests/test_worker_context.py
pytest -q
ruff check .
```

## Verified (Windows 11, Python 3.12.10, ruff 0.17.4, no Hermes installed)

- `ruff check .`: all checks passed.
- Focused run on the final head (28 files covering every touched module): 1057 passed, 5 skipped, 2 xfailed, 1 failed. The failure is `test_transcript.py::test_other_process_skips_live_capture_then_recovers_it_after_force_kill`. It also fails on `origin/main`, 6 times in 12 runs: Windows releases the killed child's file lock late.
- Full suite, run once, on the head before the last two review-fix commits: 3113 passed, 57 skipped, 5 xfailed, 13 failed, in 18 min. The failures were:
  - 11 in `test_codex_cancel_timeout.py`. 6 of them fail on `origin/main` in a single run of that file.
  - 1 in `test_codex_worker.py` (`test_lost_turn_response...`). It also fails on main (1 of 8 runs), and this branch does not touch the Codex modules.
  - The transcript force-kill test above.
  All are wall-clock or OS-timing flakes, and all reproduce on main. The last two commits (Discord guard, probe hardening) are covered by the focused run, not the full one.
- Unit-level profile isolation, using a fake multiplexed host:
  - Two profiles on one gateway each read only their own settings, key and Discord bot. Neither sees the other's values or the process environment's.
  - Concurrent turns do not cross.
  - A worker dispatched in profile A still reads A after the caller moves to B.
  - A thread that lost the turn's context fails closed.
  - Profile A's stuck catalog read neither blocks nor answers profile B, and A's late result goes only to A.
- Negative controls:
  - Against #204's original implementation, the late-result, slow-host and per-profile catalog tests fail.
  - Against #216's code, the two-profile settings and doctor tests fail.
  - Without the guard fix, the Discord host-thread guard test fails.

## Not verified

- No live multiplexed gateway receipt for this combined head. #220's body has a live two-profile receipt for its context change on its own head. #216 has none.
- No macOS or Linux run of this head. GitHub CI has not run yet.
- Still reading the process environment directly (not changed here, maintainer call): the OpenAI, Grok and GPT-Live auth resolvers (`talk_auth.resolve_auth`, `talk_grok_auth.resolve_grok_auth`, `talk_live_config.resolve_live_config`), which serve the main OpenAI realtime lane. Changing them would also change how `CODEX_HOME` and process-level keys resolve under multiplexing.
- Thread boundaries not audited: `talk_phone` notification threads, the Codex wire/worker threads and the CLI keyboard threads.
- The API verdict and capability snapshot caches are still module globals shared within one module instance (documented in `docs/BACKGROUND-WORK.md`).
- Design points left as #216 wrote them:
  - With no session profile resolved, Discord routing uses the primary bot even when `_profile_adapters` is populated.
  - `talk_config` binds Hermes's `get_secret` once, at import time.

Supersedes #216, #220 and #204.

title: fix: Discord playback completion and remote run outcomes (#218, #219)
body:
## What this lands

This PR combines two reliability fixes by @tancou into one branch on current `main` (rebased onto `a755fac`, after #244, #245 and #246). Their three commits are cherry-picked with authorship kept, followed by small maintainer commits.

### 1. Discord plays the last partial frame of a reply (#218)

Discord audio goes out in 20 ms frames. When a reply's audio did not end exactly on a frame boundary, which is most replies, the leftover piece was held back and never played. Talk counts held audio as "still speaking", so it waited forever for a quiet moment. A finished background result was therefore never announced (#239).

Now, when a reply ends, Talk marks the reply's last audio chunk. The player pads that final piece with silence, plays it, and the wait clears. The marker:

- works even when the playback queue is full,
- keeps one reply's audio separate from the next,
- is ignored for stale or duplicate "reply finished" events.

Barge-in still throws away unplayed audio. Two paths send the end-of-reply signal: the standard Discord lane (`run_talk_session`) and the native task controller. The Live controller sends it for sessions whose provider reports output turns.

### 2. Failed, cancelled and interrupted remote runs are reported as such (#219)

Before this change:

- When an api-server run ended `failed` or `cancelled`, `run_to_completion` returned ordinary text.
- Talk then recorded the run as `done` and announced "Background run #N finished."
- `interrupted` (gateway shutdown or restart) was not treated as final at all, so Talk kept polling until its time budget ran out.

Now only `completed` counts as success:

- A confirmed `failed`, `cancelled` or `interrupted` run raises a typed error carrying the remote run id and status.
- Talk records it as `failed` and keeps the remote status in the run's metadata and history.
- The announcement names the outcome: "Background run #N failed.", "... was stopped." (remote `cancelled`) or "... was interrupted.", with "the agent run cancelled: <reason>" (or failed, or interrupted) in the report.
- The status stays in the report even when a long reason is cut to the 1,500-character limit.
- The memory handoff uses the same typed outcome instead of parsing text.
- If Talk loses track of a run (network error or time budget), it says the remote outcome is unknown and keeps the run id.

Upstream `hermes-agent` uses the same four terminal statuses: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`.

### Maintainer follow-ups

- **`fix(audio): end cascade Discord replies when the TTS stream settles`.** With ElevenLabs cascade voice, the provider's "reply finished" event arrives before the TTS audio, so #218 rightly does not use it. That left the cascade lane on Discord with the same stuck tail. The Discord lane now uses CascadeVoice's existing `on_stream_end` hook as the end-of-reply signal. A barge-in still signals nothing.
- **`fix(audio): play a held Discord fragment after a bounded stall`.** GPT-Live is the only Live provider allowed on Discord. Its decoder sends audio but no output-turn event, so the #218 marker never arrives there, and the Live controller never found a quiet moment. Now, if a partial frame has waited through ten 20 ms reads with no new audio (about 200 ms), it is padded and played. The end marker stays the fast path, and arriving audio restarts the count. A stall that long is already an audible gap, so playing the fragment then costs nothing.
- **`test(audio): cover the #239 announcement path end to end`.** Runs the real Discord lane, announcement pump and delivery claim with an owed background result and a reply whose audio ends 40 bytes into a frame.
- **`test: ...`.** Asserts the typed `TalkApiRunError`, and routes the new tests' wall-clock waits through `wallclock.stretch` for Windows CI. The playback tests now call `finish_playback()` directly instead of skipping silently when it is missing.
- **`fix(runs): announce stopped and interrupted runs as such`** (maintainer decision). A run stopped with `stop_work` is announced as "Background run #N was stopped", not "failed". `talk_runs.terminal_outcome()` decides from recorded facts only: remote `cancelled` (how `stop_work`'s `POST /stop` ends) or a detached run whose process `stop_work` signalled (`meta.stop_requested`, recorded before the signal) is *stopped*; remote `interrupted` is *interrupted*; everything else non-successful is *failed*, including a lost remote outcome after a stop request. `check_work` uses the same words.
- **`docs(changelog)`.** `[Unreleased]` entries crediting @tancou for #218 and #219, plus a thank-you to the #239 reporter. `docs/OPERATING.md` describes the cascade and GPT-Live behaviour.

Fixes #239.

## Verified

- **#239 end to end.** The new test checks that:
  - the owed result waits while the tail is unplayed,
  - the next frame is the tail padded with silence,
  - `playback_pending` then clears,
  - the result is sent **exactly once**,
  - it is durably marked delivered, and another claimant cannot claim it again.

  The same test fails on `main`: there the next frame is silence and the tail is still held.
- **Cascade lane.** An 80-byte TTS tail is played padded after the stream ends. Without the follow-up, the test fails the same way.
- **GPT-Live lane.** With audio only and no turn event, the Live controller stays "busy" while the tail is held. Once the tail plays after the bound, the controller goes quiet. With the bound disabled, the new tests fail.
- **Remote outcomes.** `tests/test_api_run_terminal_status.py` (44 tests) passes here; its original 42 fail 32/42 against `main`, where `failed` and `cancelled` land as `done`.
- **Outcome wording.** Tests cover all three: a real failure says "failed"; remote `interrupted` says "was interrupted"; an operator stop says "was stopped" on both the api-server lane (stop_work → remote `cancelled`) and the detached lane (stop_work → killed child), in the announcement and in `check_work`. A detached run that dies without a delivered stop, and a stop followed by lost tracking, still say "failed". The new wording tests fail without the change.
- `ruff check .`: all checks passed (ruff 0.17.5).
- **Related test files after the final rebase:** every file that touches the changed modules, 44 files: 1644 passed, 50 skipped, 3 xfailed.
- **Full suite**, run once, before the last three commits and the rebases: 3140 passed, 57 skipped, 5 xfailed, 4 failed. All four failures are in `tests/test_codex_cancel_timeout.py`, the known Windows wall-clock flakes, in code this PR does not touch. The same file fails on `main` here too (5 failed, 19 passed). A second run of it on this branch failed 2 of 24.

All runs were on Windows 11, Python 3.12.10, offline.

## Not verified

- No live Discord call: nobody listened on a real client for the padded tail, a spoken announcement, or barge-in.
- No live ElevenLabs cascade or GPT-Live call.
- No live api-server run on this branch. The live cancellation receipt in #219 was for the contributor's own head.
- The full suite was not rerun after the bounded-stall, test-tightening and outcome-wording commits or the rebases onto #244–#246. Only the related files above were.

## Notes for review

- **The issue's offline repro.** It queues 5,000 bytes and calls `read()` three times with no end-of-reply signal. On this branch, read 1 plays the full frame and the 1,160-byte rest is still held after read 3. Read 11 plays it padded, after nine silent reads. On a lane that sends the end marker, it plays on the next read.
- **Remote `cancelled` without a Talk stop.** It is also announced as "was stopped" (upstream maps an interrupted turn to `cancelled`), since the run was stopped before finishing; the words do not say who stopped it.
- **Tuning.** `HELD_FRAGMENT_UNDERRUNS = 10` (about 200 ms) is a judgment call.

Supersedes #218 and #219.

title: feat(twilio): experimental standalone Twilio Media Streams server (#221)
body:
## What this is

An **experimental**, opt-in server that answers calls to your own Twilio number. Run `python -m talk_twilio_server` behind an HTTPS tunnel. Each inbound call gets a fresh Gemini Live voice session over Twilio Media Streams. That session has no Hermes task, no tools and no memory; it only talks.

## What it is not

- It is not the built-in Phone mode. Dograh stays the Phone mode and nothing about it changes.
- It is not loaded by normal Talk. Pressing Talk works exactly as before: nothing in the plugin, the CLI, the dashboard or `talk_phone` imports `talk_twilio`, and a test checks this.
- No new dependencies. It uses `aiohttp`, which is already a base dependency.

## Credit

The transport (µ-law codec, resampler, Media Streams parsing, TwiML, signature check, bridge) and its tests are @computator1200's work from #221. Their first commit is cherry-picked with authorship kept. Thank you!

Left out of #221:
- The ~80 unrelated test-file reformats from an older base.
- The owner/demo/memory layer. It was specific to one deployment, with a hardcoded number and a private memory server.
- The greeting turn. It relies on a Gemini 3.1 wire shape that has not been probed live yet. It can come back once a real call confirms it.
- The tool executor, because this server has no tools.

## Fixes on top (second commit)


- **Audio rate:** caller audio now goes to the session at 24 kHz, Talk's session contract. The Gemini facade downsamples 24 to 16 kHz itself, so the old 16 kHz default would have reached Gemini sped up by half.
- **Barge-in:** Twilio's buffer is also cleared on `SpeechStarted`, which is how Gemini reports barge-in outside its delegation path.
- **Dead sessions:** when the provider session ends or fails, the stream closes and the call hangs up instead of going silent.
- **Stream socket auth:** `/twilio/stream` was open to anyone. Now the signed webhook issues a single-use token, bound to the CallSid, as a TwiML `<Parameter>`. The socket opens a session only for a fresh matching token, and closes after 10 s without one.
- **Signatures:** always enforced. The unsigned bypass is gone. The signed URL is the configured public URL, so tunnels work. The webhook is POST-only, because GET would put the caller's number in the URL.
- **Callers:** `TALK_TWILIO_ALLOWED_CALLERS` is required (E.164 numbers, or `*` for anyone). Refused calls get `<Reject>`, so they are never answered or billed. Each call is capped at 15 minutes and at most 2 run at once.
- **Network:** https only for the public URL off loopback, and the server binds loopback only. There is no access log, errors log the exception type only, and the auth token is kept out of the config repr.
- **Experimental label:** shown in the module docstrings, `--help`, `--check`, `docs/TWILIO.md` and the CHANGELOG.

## Verified

- `tests/test_twilio.py` + `tests/test_twilio_server.py`: 68 passed
- `tests/test_repository_hygiene.py`, `tests/test_ui_build.py`, `tests/test_dashboard_manifest.py`: all pass (with `tests/test_register.py`: 143 passed, 3 skipped)
- `ruff check .`: clean
- Full suite (run once, before the final review fixes and the rebase; the Twilio files were rerun after both): 3143 passed, 57 skipped, 5 xfailed, 2 failed. Both failures are in `tests/test_codex_cancel_timeout.py`. That file passes 24/24 alone on this branch, and fails 3 of its tests on origin/main (a755fac), so this is the known Windows timing flake, not this change
- Ran the server locally on loopback with fake credentials. A signed webhook from an allowed number got the stream TwiML with a token, an unknown number got `<Reject>`, and an unsigned request got 403.

**No real phone call was placed**, and no Twilio or Gemini credentials were used. Real-call steps are in `docs/TWILIO.md` under *Running it*.

Supersedes #221.

title: fix: headless doctor, /talk core join, repeated fillers, echo-gate hold (#236, #215, #202, #228)
body:
Four community-reported bugs, one PR. Pressing Talk works the same as before. The one new knob is optional and off by default.

## #236: doctor and check crash on headless hosts
**Cause:** `import sounddevice` runs `Pa_Initialize()`. On a host with no PulseAudio or ALSA it raises `sounddevice.PortAudioError`, which is a plain `Exception`. `import_sounddevice()` only caught `ImportError` and `OSError`, so the error escaped through `audio_available()` into `talk_doctor._audio_check()`.
**Fix:** any other import failure now becomes `TalkAudioDeviceError` (a `TalkAudioError`). The doctor audio check, which `check` folds in, reports a warning: "terminal audio has no device: PortAudio found no audio device or sound server; Discord voice may still be usable". It no longer suggests `pip install`.

## #215: `/talk core join` offered where it cannot run
**Cause:** three places offered it with no condition: the legacy transcript contract in the session prompt, `talk_status`'s `full_parity_command`, and the Discord join, status and startup-refusal lines.
**Fix:** the prompt carries the pointer only on the Discord lane when `core_provider_available()` is true. `talk_status` reports `/talk core join (Discord voice channel only)` only when the contract exists, and `None` otherwise. The Discord lines drop the pointer on hosts without the contract. The command description now says core join is gateway-only and needs the contract. The README Background section, the README provider table (Gemini row) and the OPERATING.md "Hermes core realtime contract" section no longer describe NousResearch/hermes-agent#101808 as landed.

## #202: empty progress fillers while delegated work is pending
**Cause (Realtime lanes, terminal and Discord):** `watch_run` turned every `RunProgressWatch` milestone into a forced spoken turn ("… Tell the operator briefly."). That covered three kinds of line:
- a once-a-minute "still working" heartbeat;
- "was accepted", which repeated the WORK_STARTED receipt the model had just spoken;
- "is executing" with no label, or only the generic "Working".

Child (subagent) phases did the same.
**Cause (GPT-Live):** a delegation the model makes with no new operator speech (for example, re-checking pending work) got its refusal back as speakable commentary, so each retry was voiced as a filler. This is in `talk_native_live` and in the browser coordinator's `_empty()`.
**Fix:** the heartbeat is gone, and `accepted` and an unlabelled `executing` build no speech. Approval waits, labelled steps, results and errors are still spoken, and `check_work` still answers status questions. The phase is still recorded in run meta. On GPT-Live the no-new-input refusal is now a `kind="context"` delegation result: thinking or commentary channel instead of speakable. The browser path honors that kind. Gemini client delegation ignores the kind, so it behaves as before.

## #228: echo-gate hold for loudspeakers with latency
**Cause:** the gate decides each block from the level of the audio being written at that moment. A TV over HDMI plays it back about 200 ms later, so the model's tail reached the provider as the operator speaking.
**Fix:** a new `TALK_ECHO_GATE_HOLD_MS` setting, or **Experimental · Speaker echo hold (ms)** (`echo_gate_hold_ms`, int, default 0). It keeps the gate closed that long after playback goes quiet. During the hold, a block only has to clear the barge-in floor, so the operator can still interrupt. `0` is today's gate, byte for byte. It is documented in docs/OPERATING.md.

## Tests
Each issue has a regression test that fails on the pre-fix source and passes now:
- `test_audio`, `test_doctor` (#236)
- `test_identity`, `test_tools`, `test_cli`, `test_discord` (#215)
- `test_progress`, `test_native_live`, `test_live_coordinator`, `test_live_browser` (#202)
- `test_audio`, `test_dashboard_manifest` (#228)

Not live-verified: no provider calls were made. The GPT-Live change relies on the `context` delegation channel, which is already used for paired delegation context. #202 is marked Refs because these are the Talk-side filler sources I could find and test. Fillers the GPT-Live model produces on its own can't be ruled out without a live call, so close it after one.

Fixes #236
Fixes #215
Refs #202
Fixes #228

title: feat(discord): add opt-in same-chat delegated voice
body:
Discord users can submit work to their existing Hermes text conversation, keep talking while it runs, and hear the resulting updates without leaving the call. This draft adds the explicit `/talk delegate join` route on top of current main; ordinary `/talk join` keeps its existing behavior.

### Behavior

- Capture the invoking plugin context, profile, conversation and Discord user once. Only speech attributable to that user may submit work; text controls stay bound to the same user and chat.
- Expose two voice tools: `submit_task` and `submission_status`. Hermes chooses and executes its own tools through its normal conversation pipeline. A receipt means admission, not completion; a terminal result describes that submitted turn, not every background child it might start.
- Keep the voice conversation available while work runs. Stable request IDs recover ambiguous admissions without silently launching through another backend. Unrelated chat replies are never interpreted as a task's result.
- Read bounded context through the public persistence reader, pinned to the captured profile/session, and catch up before responses. New typed delegation-completion updates can be announced independently of submission receipts.
- Queue concise announcements until the operator and playback are idle. Interrupting speech does not cancel admitted work.
- Use a dedicated prompt describing only this route's actual tools and behavior, preserving host identity and language preferences. Versioned custom instructions use the upstream `TALK.md` loader merged in #267 (superseding #252).

### Companion API and upstream alignment

Requires [NousResearch/hermes-agent#158539](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158539), revised at `cb420ec9e0`, and the existing `allow_gateway_injection` permission. That proposal adds generic durable admission/status methods on `PluginContext`, reusing the existing authority FIFO. It does not add voice, provider or prompt policy to Agent.

This replaces this draft's earlier exact-tool host integration with a smaller delegated-work contract. The previous implementation is preserved in the fork; it is not required by this revised proposal. The branch is based on upstream `55ae7b29082faf5aaebac7cb7d692c3c2f8ade4f`, retaining the maintainer's #247 playback/cascade/GPT-Live work, #249 diagnostics and capability guidance, and #242 existing-chat routing.

The generic submission and persistence APIs are public. Audio still reuses upstream's existing private Discord adapter bridge; this draft does not claim to remove that dependency.

### Setup and limits

Send Hermes a text message to establish the conversation, join its existing Discord voice connection, set `/voice off` in that chat to avoid duplicate native TTS, then use `/talk delegate join`. Talk does not mutate or restore that setting.

This route uses the provider-owned Realtime/cascade path. GPT-Live still requires its explicit canonical-task route and is not supported by delegated join. Host-native approvals still use the host's available interface; spoken clarification does not approve a pending action.

Reset, compaction or rewritten delivered context requires leaving and rejoining. The plugin tracks at most 64 requests per call and does not adopt those receipts after a process restart. There is no cancellation, steering, resource-locking or parallel scheduler guarantee. A spoken announcement can be interrupted; ask for its result again. This is not an exactly-once audible-delivery guarantee.

### Validation

Rebased on upstream 0.25.0 (`55ae7b2`), head `a47c548`:

- Full Linux suite: **3,379 passed, 64 skipped, 5 xfailed**; Ruff and `git diff --check` pass.
- Preserves upstream custom `TALK.md` startup validation/cleanup and Discord private-catalog authorization. Tests cover custom instructions in delegated startup.
- Coverage includes receipt identity/recovery, speaker ownership, bounded context, typed completion updates and isolated bounded wait executors.
- Combined fork deployment: **152 targeted tests passed, 3 skipped**. Personal `TALK.md` remains outside this PR.

Reproduce with `pytest -q` and `ruff check .` in the documented development environment. No live microphone/provider acceptance was performed for this rebased revision. This remains draft pending the host API prerequisite and live acceptance.

### Feedback requested while draft

1. Is opt-in delegated work through the existing host conversation the preferred initial boundary, rather than exposing the host's exact tool executor to the voice provider?
2. Does the two-method companion API cover this plugin's need with the smallest useful host contract? Its description explicitly discusses convergence with other open admission/delivery proposals.
3. Should typed background delegation notices stay enabled, or should this route initially deliver only submitted-turn results and silent chat context?

Setup and semantics: [`docs/delegated-discord.md`](https://github.com/tancou/hermes-talk/blob/review/discord-canonical-upstream/docs/delegated-discord.md). Custom instructions are now upstream through #267.

title: feat(prompts): optional versioned TALK.md deployment instructions
body:
Operators maintaining several Git-based Talk deployments need persistent voice style and workflow instructions without repeating them at every join or replacing Talk's built-in execution contracts. This PR adds an optional `TALK.md` beside `talk_identity.py`, independently of the Discord proposal.

Each new Realtime or GPT-Live session reads the file and appends it to the existing host identity and voice contracts. Missing or blank files leave behavior unchanged. Content is UTF-8, bounded to 6,000 characters, and invalid/unreadable files fail startup instead of silently losing deployment instructions. Logs contain only the loaded character count. The Realtime startup path reports invalid instructions as a configuration refusal and releases any already-acquired host attachment before opening audio. Instructions influence conversational behavior; they do not grant tools, override host permissions, or prove successful execution.

The intended use is a common code branch with small, versioned deployment-specific prompt commits. For example: concise spoken responses, no repetition of a clear request, spoken clarification for missing details, and delegation of long development work with brief result announcements. **No personal deployment prompt is included in this PR.**

### Scope and design choices

- The current path is checkout-wide. Profiles sharing one plugin checkout share this prompt. Separate Git checkouts/branches can carry distinct prompts; this is not a per-profile selector.
- The convention targets source/Git deployments. Standalone wheels are not supported by this file-placement convention.
- The prompt declares deployment style/workflow preferences more specific than older remembered preferences, while honoring current operator constraints and retaining tool/host contracts. This keeps deployment preferences additive to the existing USER/MEMORY/PERSONA context rather than replacing those sections.
- The checkout-relative convention supports versioned instructions across development, preproduction and production without adding path configuration or a profile selector. Feedback on alignment with host identity conventions is welcome.
- An explicitly present but invalid file refuses startup so operators do not unknowingly run without their deployment instructions; an absent file retains the existing behavior.
- Instructions are read on new sessions only. No active-call reload, task scheduler, spoken approval bypass or change to available tools is proposed.

### Upstream reconciliation

Rebased onto the v0.24.0 main after #249, #242 and #250. The upstream core-join capability gate, language preferences and existing-chat routing remain intact. New changelog entries stay under Unreleased. The generic prompt file is still absent; deployment content stays on a separate fork branch.

### Validation

- Rebased onto upstream `d9c426ddf03e95f4239b196891fa1df23b621302` (v0.24.0 main). Linux/Python 3.12 full suite: **3296 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed**, before the additional two startup-cleanup cases. Final CLI/custom-instruction tests after those changes and English-only fixture cleanup: **81 passed**. Ruff 0.17.5 and `git diff --check` pass.
- Combined with the revised [same-chat delegated Discord proposal #251](https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-talk/pull/251) on fork branch `deploy/development-submission-0240`: **121 targeted tests passed**, followed by **5 prompt tests passed** including an added combined-contract case. The real public persistence integration also passes against the clean companion Agent branch for [NousResearch/hermes-agent#158539](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158539). This is simulated/local validation, not live voice acceptance. The combined branch preserves the delegated tool contract while appending TALK.md preferences; its deployment prompt is not part of this PR.
- All new instructions, test examples and commit messages are in English. No personal deployment file or French instructions are included in this PR's rewritten contribution history. Unicode handling remains covered with language-neutral multibyte characters.
- GitHub checks on final head `bef40586861a24706a766092ea2ea003da50dfc5` all pass: Ubuntu and Windows on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13, CodeQL, dependency review and plugin guard. Live provider acceptance has not been run.

This PR has no dependency on the Discord proposal or any unmerged Hermes Agent change. Documentation is in `docs/OPERATING.md`.

title: feat(discord): add opt-in hybrid host tools and background work
body:
## What and why

Add an opt-in `/talk hybrid join` route for a voice client that needs both short host tool operations and longer native background work in its existing Discord conversation.

For example: start a backend investigation, ask for the current branch while the child is still working, then steer that child toward a narrower scope. The short operation uses the host's exact-tool API; the long task uses native `delegate_task` with required background execution. A launch that cannot detach is refused instead of silently occupying the parent inline.

The route uses the existing speaker authorization ledger, provider session loop, delegated submission watcher, profile-pinned context reader and idle announcement behavior. The voice model gets the authorized host catalog, with `delegate_task` replaced by small launch/control tools. Ordinary `/talk join` and `/talk delegate join` retain their existing behavior.

## Dependencies and review order

This is a draft follow-up to #251, rebased on upstream 0.25.0 (`55ae7b2`). Custom `TALK.md` support is now upstream through #267, which supersedes #252. Since the upstream base is `main`, GitHub includes #251 in the current diff; commits `9545abd`, `1cd5076` and `13f427a` are the incremental hybrid changes. The revised #251 prerequisite is `a47c548`. Rebase after that prerequisite merges.

Host requirements:

- [Durable plugin submissions, Agent #158539](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158539).
- [Owned submission progress and controls, Agent #158553](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158553).
- [Exact conversation tool catalog/execution, Agent #158554](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/158554), validated head `8547b6ca5d`.

Missing host APIs or a refused catalog stop setup; there is no fallback to bare tool dispatch or a detached API-server conversation. This is a development integration, not a released-host compatibility claim. The existing private Discord audio bridge remains a separate compatibility boundary.

## Behavior and limits

- Short tools execute through the normal host tool pipeline and approvals. The parent remains a single writer: a long direct tool or ordinary `submit_task` can delay other parent operations.
- `delegate_work` starts native background children; `delegation_control` lists or requests steer/stop for an exact child. Parent `control_task` addresses only an observed submitted parent turn.
- Progress reports host facts. Queued steering is not confirmation that a model consumed it. Native Codex app-server child steering is not added; the related Agent work remains separate.
- Stable exact-call identities recover ambiguous acknowledgements. Parent controls with an unknown outcome are not automatically retried or retargeted to a new generation.
- Text and completion updates remain context, not permission. Only the initiating speaker can act. Announcements wait for idle speech/playback; interrupting audio does not cancel execution.
- Reset/compaction still requires leaving and rejoining. The call tracks at most 64 requests, with no adoption after a Talk process restart.
- This does not add spoken approval resolution or automatic child-result injection into an active host inference.

## How to test

Linux, Python 3.12, head `13f427a`:

```sh
pytest -q
ruff check .
```

**3,395 passed, 65 skipped, 5 xfailed** in the full offline suite; pinned Ruff passes. Host receipt, direct-tool and control waits use the relay-owned independent executor; startup catalog discovery also leaves the gateway default pool free. Saturation regressions exercise those paths with a one-worker default pool. To run it against the complementary Agent checkout, use that checkout's provisioned Python environment:

```sh
HERMES_AGENT_REPO=/path/to/hermes-agent \
  pytest -q tests/test_hybrid_agent_integration.py
```

The test imports the Agent PR's native integration fixture; this explicit checkout dependency is confined to opt-in test code. Production Talk uses the public context methods.

The offline provider-session tests exercise actual hybrid startup, catalog loading, the real Discord authorization ledger and relay selection: the joining speaker can execute direct/delegated operations; another speaker cannot; catalog refusal prevents provider connection. Relay tests cover fixed target/generation controls, ambiguous outcomes, duplicate IDs and strict delegation routing.

The opt-in cross-repository test passes against combined Agent runtime head `946157600d` (based on `21325a45cc`, upstream main `8da31006f3`) (receipt, controls and exact-tool branches together). It uses real admission, native agent/tool execution and persistence with controlled provider replies. It holds a native child open while a direct parent command completes, lists and steers the child, and checks that the next child inference contains the correction. It also checks duplicate exact-call recovery. The probe's speaker authorization is stubbed; the provider-session tests exercise the actual ledger separately.

The cross-repository integration passed again against the rebased Talk deployment (`6b32c7e`). Upstream custom-instruction startup cleanup and Discord private-catalog protection are preserved. Live microphone/provider audio, Discord reconnect and spoken approvals have not been validated. Draft feedback on the command/API shape is welcome before promoting this integration.

## Platforms

- [x] Linux
- [ ] Windows
- [ ] macOS

## Live receipt

Not yet supplied. The required live delegation/audio acceptance remains outstanding; this PR intentionally stays draft until that receipt is available. Offline tests are not presented as a live `hermes talk check --json` receipt.

## Checklist

- [x] One hybrid integration; tests included in the same commit.
- [x] Full offline suite and pinned Ruff pass.
- [x] Conventional commit, English public text and documentation.
- [x] No auth-store or credential-routing change; fixtures contain no credentials or user transcripts.
- [x] Narration distinguishes admission, execution, control requests and completion.
- [x] README, operating/voice-command docs and credited changelog entry updated.
- [ ] Live delegation/audio receipt (required before requesting final acceptance).

title: feat: experimental Discord auto-join and OpenAI-compatible cascade TTS (#224, #151)
body:
Two community-requested features, both **Experimental and off by default**. Pressing Talk behaves exactly as before, and there are no new dependencies.

## Discord auto-join (#224, requested by @Akm0d)
- Turn on *Experimental · Discord auto-join* or set `TALK_DISCORD_AUTO_JOIN=1`. When the bot is not yet in voice on that server, `/talk join` then joins **the caller's** voice channel through the host's own `get_user_voice_channel` / `join_voice_channel`, and starts Talk.
- Works only for users in `TALK_DISCORD_OPERATOR_USER_IDS` (an empty list refuses). Uses the invoking profile's bot only (#185).
- Refuses clearly when the caller is not in voice, when run from a DM, or when the bot lacks Connect/Speak permission. An existing connection is reused and never moved.
- Talk closes only a connection it opened, either when the start refuses or raises, or when the session ends. If `/voice join` adopted that connection in the meantime, it is left to the host. Overlapping joins are serialized.
- With the knob off, the `start_session` call is byte-identical to before.

## OpenAI-compatible cascade TTS (#151, requested by @HearthCore)
- `TALK_CASCADE_TTS=openai` sends one `POST {base}/audio/speech` per sentence chunk over the existing `aiohttp`. `pcm` audio streams straight to the sink; `wav` must be 24 kHz mono 16-bit.
- Configure with `TALK_CASCADE_OPENAI_BASE_URL`, `_MODEL` and `_VOICE` (required), plus `_API_KEY` and `_FORMAT` (optional), or the matching Experimental settings.
- Plain `http://` is refused off loopback, as are credentials, queries or fragments in the URL. Redirects are not followed.
- The key is sent only in the `Authorization` header and never falls back to `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- The chunker, barge-in and the text-only fallback are inherited unchanged. The doctor covers the new backend. ElevenLabs stays the default, and existing callers still get the `(key, voice, model)` triple.
- Backends now plug in through `build_cascade_voice`, so an edge-tts adapter (#127) would be one subclass plus one registry entry. It is not added here.

## Docs
- `docs/OPERATING.md`: new sections for both features.
- `CHANGELOG.md` [Unreleased]: Added lines with credits.
- `plugin.yaml`: 5 new "Experimental · …" settings, using loader-known types only.

## Tests
- New: `tests/test_cascade_openai_tts.py` and `tests/test_discord_auto_join.py`. They cover defaults unchanged, the enabled paths, the refusals, barge-in, overlapping joins and failed starts.
- Focused run: 455 passed, 3 skipped, 2 xfailed. Files run: the two new ones, `test_cascade_voice`, `test_dashboard_cascade`, `test_discord_cascade`, `test_discord`, `test_register`, `test_doctor`, `test_dashboard_manifest`, `test_ui_build` and `test_operator_auth`.
- `ruff check .` is clean.

Closes #224
Closes #151

title: Release 0.25.0: run Hermes workflows by voice
body:
## What changed

Adds on-demand discovery of the active Hermes bot’s skills, plugins, tools and commands. Unbound OpenAI Realtime in Desktop can invoke an eligible native workflow from a fresh spoken request with “slash NAME” or “run the slash NAME command”. The new lookup adds zero classifier calls. This PR also sets the package and manifests to 0.25.0.

## Verification

The operator installed commit `1525f6d` on an everyday Windows Hermes Desktop profile and confirmed the real microphone test worked on a Codex subscription. title: gpt-4o-mini-tts is retired by OpenAI on 6 January 2027
body:
Hi! A heads-up in case it's useful:

OpenAI removes `gpt-4o-mini-tts` from the API on 6 January 2027 ([OpenAI deprecations page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)). After that date, calls to it fail.
`gpt-4o-mini-tts` is used here: https://github.com/TheSmokeDev/hermes-talk/blob/main/talk_providers.py#L38
OpenAI's recommended replacement (as of 20 November 2026): `gpt-4o-mini-tts` → `gpt-realtime-2.1-mini`. Current advice, kept up to date: https://aidriftline.com/models/gpt-4o-mini-tts/

Note: moving off it is more than a new model name. OpenAI calls this a change of API workflow: the replacement isn't a model for /v1/audio/speech and runs through the Realtime API. (guide: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/text-to-speech)

A new model can answer the same prompt differently (format, length, JSON), so it may be worth running a few real prompts on it before switching.

(I found this with a small scanner I built for these dates, in case you want to check the rest of the repo: `npx -y @aidriftline/driftline .`)

title: Gemini lane: `gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking` closes with 1007 at setup, and with a thinking level its tool calls never reach the client
body:
### Where

Terminal lane, v0.25.0 (55ae7b2), `TALK_PROVIDER=gemini`, AI Studio key. Tested on 23/11/2026 with the plugin's own `talk_gemini_realtime.build_setup_message()` over a raw socket, so the setup payload is exactly what Talk sends.

### 1. Setup is refused

With `TALK_GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-3.8-live-extended-thinking`, the setup Talk builds is closed immediately:

```
1007 Thinking level must be specified for this model.
```

It's the same close code as #227, but a different cause: `build_setup_message()` never sends `generationConfig.thinkingConfig`. Adding `"thinkingConfig": {"thinkingLevel": "low"}` (`"LOW"` and `"high"` also work) gets `setupComplete`.

### 2. With a thinking level, tool calls never reach the client

Same tool and question that work on `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` and `gemini-3.8-live` (`get_weather`, "What is the weather in Rio de Janeiro in celsius?"):

- The model says "Let me check the weather for you."
- It ends the turn with `"turnComplete": true, "interactionStatus": "IN_PROGRESS"`. `interactionStatus` is a field I haven't seen on the other models.
- **No `toolCall` frame is ever sent**, nor any `toolCallCancellation` or `error` frame.
- A second turn follows on its own: "I'm sorry, but a system error occurred and I couldn't retrieve the weather details", ending with `interactionStatus: "IDLE"`.

The result was the same with four tool declarations:
- the closed schema from #227 in `parametersJsonSchema`;
- a plain `{"city": string}` in `parametersJsonSchema`;
- the same plain schema in OpenAPI `parameters`;
- `"behavior": "NON_BLOCKING"`.

So it doesn't look schema-related. My guess is that this model runs function calls through some server-side interaction flow that the Live client protocol doesn't expose, but I couldn't confirm that.

### Suggestion

- Send `thinkingConfig.thinkingLevel` for models that require it, e.g. a `TALK_GEMINI_THINKING_LEVEL` setting, or a default for `*-extended-thinking` models.
- Until tool calls work there, have `talk doctor` warn that this model can't run Hermes tools. Otherwise the agent tells the user that "a system error occurred", which reads like a Hermes failure.

Related, from reading the code (not verified live): `GeminiLiveSession.connect()` only sets `_live_context_transport` for `gemini-2.5-*` and `gemini-3.1-*`. On `gemini-3.8-live`, which works fine for tool calls, live context updates (task continuity) would therefore be off. Worth adding `gemini-3.8-` if 3.8 uses the same transport as 3.1.

Happy to test a branch against these models.

title: fix(local): declare 24 kHz PCM in the session update
body:
## What and why

The local lane (`TALK_PROVIDER=local`) sends the OpenAI GA session update with no `audio.input.format` or `audio.output.format`. Against OpenAI that's fine, because the GA default is `audio/pcm` at 24 kHz, exactly what Talk captures and plays (`talk_audio.SAMPLE_RATE`). huggingface/speech-to-speech 1.1.0 instead falls back to its **16 kHz** pipeline rate when the client states no format (`PIPELINE_SAMPLE_RATE = 16000`, `api/openai_realtime/handlers/audio.py`). So:

- **Output:** the server sends 16 kHz PCM and Talk plays it at 24 kHz. Replies come out 1.5x fast and pitched up. Our operator described it as "Alvin and the Chipmunks".
- **Input:** Talk's 24 kHz microphone audio is read as 16 kHz, 1.5x slow and pitched down. Parakeet still transcribed Portuguese, but from a distorted signal.

`talk_local_realtime.build_session_update()` now declares `{"type": "audio/pcm", "rate": 24000}` on both directions. The `default` voice is still omitted, so the server keeps its own speaker. The OpenAI lane is unchanged. No spoken sentence changes.

Found while testing the local lane on Linux + AMD. A related speech-to-speech problem, a mid-conversation system item hoisted into the system prompt, is filed upstream as huggingface/speech-to-speech#870. I'm opening a separate issue here for its effect on Talk's announcements.

## How to test

```bash
pytest -q tests/test_local_realtime.py
# new: test_session_update_declares_the_24khz_pcm_talk_actually_uses
#      fails on main, passes here
```

Live measurement against speech-to-speech 1.1.0 (Kokoro `pf_dora`). The same sentence ("um, dois, três, quatro, cinco, seis, sete, oito") was requested with Talk's own `build_session_update()`, with and without the two format keys:

| session update | audio bytes received | duration played at 24 kHz |
|---|---|---|
| main | 95,232 | 1.98 s (actual speech: 2.98 s) |
| this PR | 142,848 | 2.98 s |

The ratio is exactly 1.5. With the format declared, the server's own `StreamingPcm16Resampler` takes over.

## Platforms

- [ ] Windows
- [x] Linux: Ubuntu 24.04, Ryzen 7 5700X, AMD Radeon RDNA4 (PCI 1002:7590), no CUDA. Parakeet TDT and Kokoro on CPU, LLM `gemma-4-26b-a4b` (UD-Q4_K_XL) on llama.cpp/llama-swap on the GPU via `--llm_backend chat-completions`.
- [ ] macOS

`docs/LOCAL.md` only lists a Windows/NVIDIA verification, so this is a second data point. With `--responses_api_reasoning_effort none`, Gemma 4 picked a tool in 1.3–2.2 s, against 11–23 s with reasoning on.

## Live receipt

`hermes talk check --provider local --json` on the installed v0.25.0. Profile name redacted, plugin/host detail trimmed.

```json
{"command": "hermes talk check", "ok": true, "provider": "local", "schema_version": 1,
 "steps": [
  {"id": "static", "status": "pass", "summary": "doctor: 8 pass, 3 warn, 0 fail"},
  {"id": "provider_session", "status": "pass", "summary": "local local answered one text turn (29696 audio bytes)",
   "details": {"audio_bytes": 29696, "auth_source": "env", "events": 11, "model": "local", "provider": "local",
               "response_finished": true, "session_ready": true, "transcript_chars": 6, "voice": "default"}},
  {"id": "hermes_run", "status": "pass", "summary": "run #25 on the detached lane echoed HERMES_TALK_CHECK_OK"}],
 "summary": {"fail": 0, "pass": 3, "skip": 0}}
```

This receipt is from main, and it passes there too: `talk check` counts audio bytes, not their rate, so it can't see this bug. I haven't installed the patched plugin and listened to it. The evidence for the fix is the byte measurement above, taken with this PR's `build_session_update()`.

## Checklist

- [x] One logical change; tests ride with it, not behind it
- [x] `pytest -q` (3360 passed, 63 skipped, 5 xfailed) and `ruff check .` (0.17.5) pass locally
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits with a hermes-talk scope (`fix(local): …`)

title: local lane + speech-to-speech: task results are never spoken; the previous sentence is repeated instead
body:
### What the operator experiences

Local lane, terminal, v0.25.0, speech-to-speech 1.1.0, `gemma-4-26b-a4b` via llama.cpp. The operator asks for a task, for example "search my GitHub e-mails from today", and Talk delegates it:
- The delegated run **finishes**: run done at 16:32:05, 2 e-mails found.
- A few seconds later Talk speaks again, but it says **the same sentence as before, word for word** ("Yes, the search is still in progress, I'll tell you when it's done").
- The result is never spoken, so from the operator's side the task never completes.

It happened twice in one session, once for each delegated task.

### Cause

Talk delivers the result as `AddContext(role=system)` + `StartResponse(allow_tools=False)` + `RemoveContext` (`_announcement_commands` in `talk_cli.py`). speech-to-speech doesn't keep a system item at its position in the conversation:

- `Chat._add_item_locked()` stores any system item as the chat's `init_chat_message`, the single leading system prompt (`LLM/chat.py`; same code on current `main`). A second system item replaces the first.
- The request sent to the LLM is therefore `[system: instructions + announcement, …, assistant: "<previous sentence>"]`, so it **ends with an assistant message**.
- llama.cpp's server treats a trailing assistant message as a prefill: it continues it and returns the prefill plus the continuation. Gemma emits EOS immediately (`completion_tokens: 1`), and the response content is the previous sentence.
- speech-to-speech speaks that content, which is the repetition the operator hears.

Reproduced three ways:

| request | result |
|---|---|
| through speech-to-speech, announcement as `system` (Talk today) | 1 output token, previous sentence re-spoken |
| through speech-to-speech, the same announcement as a `user` item | 46 tokens: "I found two e-mails from today mentioning GitHub: …" |
| direct to llama.cpp, announcement at the end as `system`, `user` or `developer` | all three spoken correctly |
| direct to llama.cpp, announcement hoisted into the leading system prompt (what s2s sends) | 1 token, previous sentence returned |

So the model can handle the announcement. It just never reaches the end of the conversation.

### Where to fix

The root fix belongs in speech-to-speech: keep mid-conversation system items in order. Reported there as huggingface/speech-to-speech#870. (The same session also had 1.5x-fast "chipmunk" audio from an undeclared sample rate; that one is fixed in #281.) On the Talk side, a few ideas, though you know the trade-offs better:

- **Delivery of announcements on the local lane:** sending them as a `user` item would work here, but it gives quoted run output the operator's authority. That's exactly what the system role and the "DATA, not instructions" framing avoid, so I wouldn't do it blindly.
- **Docs:** add this to `docs/LOCAL.md` ("Limits") until speech-to-speech handles it.
- **Echo guard:** a response whose text equals the previous assistant turn is a strong signal of this failure, and could be logged.

### Also in `docs/LOCAL.md`

"Run the bundled multi-turn check before trusting a new model" refers to a check that isn't in the repo, or in its history since #208. I wrote a small one: the six steps from the doc, with Talk's real `default_talk_tools()` and `build_instructions()` over the local socket, in Brazilian Portuguese. Result for `gemma-4-26b-a4b` with reasoning off: 5/6.
- Delegate, delegate, progress, stop and small talk were correct, with 1–3 s per decision (7 s on the first, cold turn).
- For "create a reminder" it called `talk_capabilities` first instead of delegating.

Happy to contribute it as `scripts/` or a test if useful.

### Real-session latencies (CPU STT/TTS, GPU LLM)

From the server log of a 7-minute spoken session:

| stage | range |
|---|---|
| STT (Parakeet, CPU) | 0.6–2.2 s |
| LLM (Gemma 4, GPU, reasoning off) | 1.1–5.4 s |
| first audio (Kokoro, CPU) | 2.7–6.7 s |
| end to end | 6–17 s |

Kokoro on CPU is the slowest part.

title: OpenAI lane: finished-run announcements are never seen by the model, because the self-delete in the same batch is applied first
body:
### What the operator experiences

Terminal, v0.25.0, `TALK_PROVIDER=openai`, `gpt-realtime-2.1` on the ChatGPT subscription (Codex OAuth). The operator delegates two tasks:

| task | run done | `talk-runs.jsonl` delivery |
|---|---|---|
| weather | 17:07:20 | `delivered` at 17:07:22 |
| e-mail search | 17:07:20 | `delivered` at 17:07:39 |

The model's spoken reply to each announcement was:
- "I don't have a new update yet, neither on the e-mails nor on the forecast…"
- "I still don't have the result of the e-mail search…"

The results only reached the operator when they asked again and the model called `check_work`.

### Cause

`_announcement_commands()` sends `AddContext(system)` + `StartResponse(allow_tools=False)` + `RemoveContext` **in one batch**. Its docstring assumes "the response snapshots conversation state at creation; the delete only shapes what FUTURE turns see". On the OpenAI GA endpoint that's not what happens: the `conversation.item.delete` is applied before the model reads the conversation, so the response is generated without the report.

### A/B on the same session shape

Talk's own `run_finished_commands()` with a real run output, Talk's real tools and instructions, `gpt-realtime-2.1`, 23/11/2026:

| how the announcement is sent | what the model says | runs |
|---|---|---|
| as Talk does today (delete in the same batch) | "I can't access your e-mail from here…" (report not seen) | 2/2 |
| without the delete | "No GitHub notifications today; one marketing e-mail mentions GitHub; the last notifications are from 21/11…" | 2/2 |
| delete sent **after** `response.done` | "The background work has finished. As data: no GitHub notifications received today…" | 2/2 |

The script is below. It mints with Codex OAuth and drives the socket directly with `talk_cli.run_finished_commands()`.

### Suggested fix

Keep all three containments (system role, no tools, item doesn't persist), but send the `conversation.item.delete` when that announcement's `response.done` arrives, not in the same batch. The window in which the report exists is then one tools-disabled response, which is what the docstring intends. An alternative is an out-of-band `response.create` with `conversation: "none"` and the report in `input`, which needs no delete at all. Talk already uses that shape for the core render path.

The Gemini lane is probably not affected (its context delete is already degraded to local handling), and the local lane has a different problem with system items (#282, speech-to-speech hoists them).

### Also seen in the same session

These aren't a separate bug, but they're for the #202 family.
- **Preambles before tool calls:** "Okay, let me think about how to answer that in the most useful way", "Good question, let me quickly explain what's happening".
- **Updates with no news:** after each lost announcement, the model filled in with "no update yet" lines. Fixing the delete removes the trigger for those.
- **Noise turns:** two short noise fragments were transcribed as "Hola." and "作" (CJK), and each got a full spoken reply. This is with the echo gate floor at 0.08 on a TV speaker.

Barge-in worked on this lane: the operator interrupted mid-sentence and the model followed. On the Gemini lane, with the same gate settings, it didn't. I haven't isolated why. A likely candidate is that the Live protocol has no client cancel/truncate (as documented in `talk_gemini_realtime.py`), while OpenAI does.

<details><summary>A/B script (run with the plugin's own venv; needs a Codex login)</summary>

```python
"""A/B do aviso de tarefa concluída na integração OpenAI Realtime (assinatura via Codex).

O Talk manda o resultado como: AddContext(system) + response.create(tool_choice none)
+ conversation.item.delete do mesmo item, no MESMO lote. No teste falado de
23/11/2026 o modelo respondeu "ainda não tenho atualização" aos dois avisos.
Aqui: o mesmo aviso, com o resultado real da tarefa #22, com e sem o delete.

Uso: python anuncio-openai-ab.py PASTA_DO_PLUGIN
"""
import asyncio, json, sys

plugin = sys.argv[1]; sys.path.insert(0, plugin)
import aiohttp  # noqa: E402
import talk_auth, talk_wire, talk_tools, talk_identity, talk_cli  # noqa: E402
import talk_realtime as rt, talk_openai_realtime as oa  # noqa: E402

MODEL = "gpt-realtime-2.1"
TOOLS = talk_tools.default_talk_tools()
INSTR = talk_identity.build_instructions(None, tools=TOOLS, lane="cli")
SAIDA = ("Resultado da busca — hoje, 23/11/2026: NÃO há nenhuma notificação do GitHub recebida hoje. "
         "Há um e-mail de marketing (Chester Flake, '30 new Microsoft bootcamps') que cita GitHub. "
         "As últimas notificações do GitHub são de 21/11, do repositório TheSmokeDev/hermes-talk (PR #245 e issues #227/#228/#229).")


async def rodada(com_delete):  # True = mesmo lote; False = sem delete; "depois" = delete após response.done
    auth = talk_auth.resolve_auth(env={})
    desc = talk_wire.mint_ephemeral_session(auth_token=auth.token, model=MODEL, voice="marin",
                                            instructions=INSTR, tools=TOOLS)
    url = f"{talk_wire.OPENAI_REALTIME_WS_URL}?model={MODEL}"
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as http:
        async with http.ws_connect(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {desc.client_secret}"}) as ws:
            async def enviar(*cmds):
                for c in cmds:
                    await ws.send_json(c if isinstance(c, dict) else oa.encode_command(c))

            async def ate_fim():
                fala, calls = [], []
                while True:
                    m = await ws.receive(timeout=90)
                    if m.type != aiohttp.WSMsgType.TEXT:
                        return " ".join(fala), calls, f"[socket {m.type}]"
                    ev = json.loads(m.data); tp = ev.get("type", "")
                    if tp.endswith("audio_transcript.done") or tp == "response.output_text.done":
                        fala.append(ev.get("transcript") or ev.get("text") or "")
                    elif tp == "response.output_item.done" and ev["item"].get("type") == "function_call":
                        calls.append(ev["item"])
                    elif tp == "error":
                        fala.append(f"[ERRO {ev['error'].get('message')}]")
                    elif tp == "response.done":
                        return " ".join(fala), calls, ev["response"].get("status")

            await enviar(rt.AddInputText(item_id="u1", text="Pesquise meus e-mails do GitHub de hoje."), rt.StartResponse())
            fala, calls, _ = await ate_fim()
            for _ in range(3):
                if not calls:
                    break
                for c in calls:
                    nome = c["name"]
                    out = ("Started run #22 in the background." if nome == "delegate_task"
                           else "No dedicated e-mail tool; delegate it." if nome == "talk_capabilities" else "ok")
                    await enviar({"type": "conversation.item.create", "item": {
                        "type": "function_call_output", "call_id": c["call_id"], "output": out}})
                await enviar(rt.StartResponse())
                fala, calls, _ = await ate_fim()
            print(f"  antes do aviso: «{fala[:120]}»")
            run = {"runId": 22, "status": "done", "output": SAIDA, "meta": {}}
            cmds = talk_cli.run_finished_commands(run)  # exatamente o que o Talk manda
            depois = [c for c in cmds if isinstance(c, rt.RemoveContext)]
            if com_delete is not True:
                cmds = [c for c in cmds if not isinstance(c, rt.RemoveContext)]
            await enviar(*cmds)
            fala, _, status = await ate_fim()
            if com_delete == "depois":
                await enviar(*depois)
            rotulo = {True: "delete no mesmo lote (Talk hoje)", False: "sem delete", "depois": "delete após response.done"}[com_delete]
            print(f"  AVISO ({rotulo}): «{fala[:200]}» [{status}]")


async def main():
    for com in (sys.argv[2:] and [{'mesmo': True, 'sem': False, 'depois': 'depois'}[a] for a in sys.argv[2:]] or (True, False, True, False)):
        await rodada(com)

asyncio.run(main())
```
